cards.title: Native debugger: DAP framing and state-machine core
cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#12:0] Split from the former #12 umbrella. This card owns only “Native debugger: DAP framing and state-machine core.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #12. The other 6 delivery slices have separate cards.

log.text: Rebalanced former umbrella into #12, #797, #798, #799, #800, #801, #802. Each card owns one delivery slice.

Heads-up for planning: after D-ONECORE1=A (#778), jet run stacks can mix native Cranelift frames and interpreter (tier-0) frames. The native DAP backend must present mixed-tier stacks coherently — plan a frame-provenance seam, not lldb-only assumptions.
Fresh-review repair: expanded #12 to the complete ratified D-DBG-DAP1=A lifecycle, capability, attach, privacy, schema, client, and conformance contract; corrected tests/debug.rs criteria.
E8 planning rebase: shipped native/DAP backend credited; residual narrowed to live DAP lifecycle, editor wiring, bounded cleanup, and exact support docs. No new gate.
Owner moved remaining editor/platform debugger interoperability and native cross-platform CI proof to E8 CI & Documentation; shipped debugger core stays credited.
Reopened by 2026-07-09 universal audit: no real VS Code/Zed DAP acceptance or editor wiring; adapter is minimal/one-threaded; Windows and full breakpoint/evaluate/exception/task paths remain.

[handoff] lldb added to flake.nix devShells.default.packages (was an ad-hoc nixpkgs fetch for verification only). `nix develop -c which lldb` resolves; tests/debug_native.rs's live-gated case reruns clean (5/5 ok, 1.90s) with no manual PATH workaround. The Open Owner-Q ask below is now resolved — owner said add it.

[done] Native lldb backend shipped end-to-end and verified against a REAL live lldb (fetched via nixpkgs for this session; not yet in flake.nix devShell — see Open Owner-Q). Codegen: TStmt::LineMarker + emit_bundle_dbg/compile_for_debug emit `// jet:line N` markers gated by cx.debug_linemap (off by default — zero effect on normal builds, golden tests, or the JIT tier; confirmed via full test suite + `cargo test --workspace` diffing). New Source/Debug/{LineMap,Inferior,Native,Dap}.rs. `jet debug` auto-dispatches interpreter vs native via the SAME E2203 boundary scan (needs_native) — one command, one meaning (I8); `--dap` forces native for editor launch; `--raw-frames` (D-DBG2) shows raw Rust file:line. Reuses the exact ratified (jet) vocabulary (D-DBG3) over both backends. Live-lldb verification surfaced and fixed THREE real bugs a docs-only implementation would have shipped broken: (1) lldb never re-prints a bare prompt over a pipe (echoes command instead) — naive prompt-wait hangs forever, fixed with a sentinel-command read loop; (2) a resume command's own stop banner is asynchronous and can lose a race to the NEXT command's reply — fixed by always deriving position from a synchronous follow-up `bt`, never the resume's own text; (3) the debuggee inherits lldb's stdout by default, so a Jet `print()` can tear a control-channel sentinel in half — fixed by redirecting debuggee stdout/stderr to temp files via `settings set target.output/error-path` and draining them into the transcript. Also loads rustc's own Rust pretty-printer (lldb_lookup.py + lldb_commands, same two files rust-lldb loads) so String/&str locals render as `"text"` instead of raw allocator internals. Tests: 12 new unit tests (LineMap/Inferior, no lldb needed) + tests/debug_native.rs (5 tests, gated on lldb presence like tests/observe.rs gates on rustc — skips clean without it). New example examples/features/189_debug_native.jet (native-only via `use core.fs`) + golden .out. Full regression pass: cargo build/test workspace-relevant targets (debug, debug_native, golden, observe, cli, tir, decisions, dev/JIT) all green. NOT done: DAP JSON-over-stdio server (Dap.rs) is implemented to the documented wire spec but UNTESTED against a real editor (no VS Code/Zed available here) — verify before wiring into editors/zed or vscode launch configs. gdb/Windows explicitly out of scope (phase 1 = lldb/Linux, per the plan).
Pulled back into e3 per owner: IDE tooling is an E3 exit criterion and this closes it (native DAP/lldb backend + editor wiring). e7 tag on 2026-06-30 was a batch sweep, not a deliberate re-exclude.
Activated into epoch e7 track

No open decision (lldb is a runtime TOOL dep, not an I6 compiler crate; the interpreter is the no-lldb fallback — baked, not balloted). TO BUILD step-2: a native DAP/lldb backend that steps the FULL feature set the interpreter declines (E2203: FFI, tasks, #Unsafe, native std) + the D-DBG2 --raw-frames expert view + editor DAP wiring. Plan: dap-debugger. VERIFY: stepping a program that uses FFI/tasks (which the interpreter refuses with E2203) through the native backend.

cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#218:0] Split from the former #218 umbrella. This card owns only “Self-hosting: compiler seam inventory and retained-host boundary.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #218. The other 9 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Inventory every compiler seam the self-host port must preserve, and name the retained-host boundary: what stays Rust/host-only versus what must become Jet-authored behind a stable internal ABI.

## Scope
In: seam catalog (driver, lexer, parser, sema, TIR lower, codegen lenses, queries, diagnostics, CLI); retained-host list with reasons; ABI/ownership rules for crossing the boundary; proof that no third lens or parallel front-end is introduced.
Out: actual port work (#808–#816, #671+); TIR freeze prose (#668); speed bets (#669); behavioral comparator (#670).

## Law
- R12 / D-ONECORE1=A: one semantic core, exhaustive consumers, no third lens.
- I2: rustc stays hidden; host seams must not leak as user diagnostics.
- I6: compiler seams stay path-dependency clean.

## Owned paths
- `docs/spec/architecture.md` (seam inventory section or linked table)
- `Source/lib.rs`, `crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs`
- crate roots under `crates/jet-*` as cited evidence
- focused inventory test or lint that fails when a new seam appears undocumented (if practical); otherwise checklist criteria + review

## Steps
1. Wait for owner reopen of frozen #217 (bootstrap readiness gate).
2. Walk driver → lexer → parser → sema → TIR → JIT/AOT lenses → queries → diagnostics → CLI; record each public/internal seam.
3. Mark each seam: Jet-portable now / later / retained-host forever (with reason).
4. Specify ownership, panic containment, and version lock rules for any C-ABI or host call.
5. Diff against sibling port cards so no seam is owned twice or left orphaned.
6. Independent review against criteria.

## Acceptance / proof
Criteria 1–3. Proof: architecture doc table + review; no implementation of ports on this card.

## Blockers

cards.body:
Integration closeout only. Broad implementation remains on existing focused child cards. This card owns reconciliation of their evidence and removal of duplicate paths.

Original context:
Ratified decision: D-WD14 = B (Typed budgets (recommended)).
Source ballot: docs/ballots/world-domination-review-2026-07-06.md.

Whether performance expectations are declared and enforced as product facts.

Chosen direction: Budgets attach to packages/envs/services and feed build, bench, dev, dossier, and CI. Weakness fixed: deterministic budgets are hard gates; statistical budgets use pinned baselines and trend policy.

Guardrails:
- Preserve magic defaults plus full expert control from the ballot.
- Before adding any new user-typeable syntax, manifest field, command spelling, marker, provider prefix, or diagnostic code, raise a follow-up Tower ballot.
- No implementation card may ship a stub: docs, examples, diagnostics, tests, and verification must land with behavior.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.http — client/server parity with Go net/http + requests ergonomics
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go net/http server completeness with Python requests/httpx client ergonomics. Client HTTPS-by-default (D-TLS1) and server TLS (D-TLSSERVE1) shipped — audit the rest.

Client gaps to audit: connection pooling/keep-alive; redirect policy control; cookie jar; multipart upload and form encoding; streaming request and response bodies (bounded memory); per-phase timeouts (connect/read/total); proxy support (env-standard); transparent gzip decompression; HTTP/2; typed URL input (consumes the core.url card).

Server gaps to audit: router with path params and wildcards; middleware chain; streaming responses and server-sent events; graceful shutdown; request size/time limits (safe defaults — I1); static file serving with range requests; access logging via core.log.

WebSocket client + server: likely its own module name (owner ballot). Done means: audit table plus shipped gaps with example servers/clients under golden tests; a realistic REST service example needs no third-party anything. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Finish D-HTTPDEPTH1/A on typed core.url/core.mime/core.net: Client/Server/Router/middleware, pooling/keepalive, redirects, cookies, forms/multipart, bounded streaming, phase timeouts, proxy, compression, TLS, SSE, limits, static ranges, logging, and graceful shutdown. Apply HTTP-CORE2/CLIENT2/SERVER2 and D-DEP-HTTP2=B exactly. HTTP/2 is a transport upgrade; WebSocket lives only in core.ws per D-WS1=B. Prove hostile protocol framing, smuggling/limits/disconnects, real client/server/browser interop, AOT/dev parity, examples/docs, and no facade.

cards.body:
Integration closeout only. Broad implementation remains on existing focused child cards. This card owns reconciliation of their evidence and removal of duplicate paths.

Original context:
Best-in-class bar: polars/pandas essentials, kept typed and deterministic (Jet's selectors are typed lambdas — misspelled columns are compile errors; keep that advantage everywhere). Current: csv<T>, count/sum/mean/min/max, group_count/sum/mean, bar_text/bar_svg. Reconcile with epoch-3/typed-data-core.md before adding scope.

Gaps: filter/select/sort pipelines over [T]; joins (inner/left) on typed keys; pivot; median/quantiles/std/variance; describe summary; rolling/window aggregations; datetime columns (consumes the core.time card); Parquet and Arrow IO (bridge gates — owner ballots); lazy pipeline evaluation decision (ship or record non-goal).

Done means: an analysis example (load CSV → join → group → plot) ships under golden tests; audit table records non-goals. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

cards.title: Comptime parity inventory and transcript closeout
cards.body:
Integration closeout only. Broad implementation remains on existing focused child cards. This card owns reconciliation of their evidence and removal of duplicate paths.

Original context:
Owner hit this live (2026-07-09): `big :: BigInt(100)` in jet repl fails with E0956 "calling BigInt can't run at compile time yet", while examples/features/text/bigint.jet (D-BIGINT1=A, golden) runs fine AOT. The REPL executes through the comptime interpreter (tier-0), so every builtin the AOT backend supports but comptime doesn't is a user-visible parity break — R12 requires JIT/dev/REPL parity through the same executable TIR.

Scope:
1. Implement BigInt construction + arithmetic + to_string in the comptime interpreter (crates/jet-comptime; CtValue may need a BigInt variant — check how AOT lowers it first).
2. Audit: enumerate every builtin/Core call AOT supports vs the comptime whitelist; produce the parity matrix as a test (ui or dedicated tests/parity.rs) so new builtins can't ship AOT-only. E0956 sites are the search key.
3. Each fixed gap needs a repl transcript test; keep E0956 wording for genuinely impossible-at-comptime effects only.

Repro: printf 'big :: BigInt(100)\n:quit\n' | target/debug/jet repl

cards.body: Build a React/SvelteKit/Next-class Jet-native application platform by composing the already-ratified Router, reactive state, typed UI/style/a11y, event, HTTP, and web backend mechanisms. Scope: one application graph; single-file and multi-file authoring; nested routing/data/actions/forms; CSR/SSR/SSG/streaming; hydration/islands; security, assets, code splitting, caching, adapters, real-browser HMR/devtools, accessibility, and production dogfood. cards.title: TIR spec freeze — the lens contract for self-hosting
cards.body: R12 and D-VERDICT-666-1 require exactly two feature-identical lenses: JIT and optimized AOT, both consuming one executable TIR. Self-hosting changes the front end that produces TIR; it does not add a third consumer or lens. This card records and machine-enforces that internal contract from canonical source before port work begins, without a serialized schema or speculative version framework.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Freeze the semantic-core TIR contract that self-hosting must produce and that every engine must consume exhaustively (D-ONECORE1=A / R12).

## Law
- One semantic-core TIR (post-#776 / D-ONECORE1=A), not emission-shaped legacy TIR.
- Exactly two feature-identical lenses: JIT and optimized AOT; interpreter is reference semantics.
- No serialization, version tags, or migration machinery on this card.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs` and exhaustive consumers stay canonical; `docs/spec/tir.md` documents without a second source of truth.

## Scope
In: `docs/spec/tir.md` totality/sema-ownership/lowering/consumer laws; strengthen exhaustive-match and differential tests so a new executable node cannot land without every engine handling it.
Out: porting front ends; speed corpus (#666/#669); byte-identical stage builds (#814/#815).

## Owned paths
- `docs/spec/tir.md` (create or extend)
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/{mod,lower,emit,subset}.rs`
- exhaustive-match / differential tests for interpreter + lenses
- architecture cross-links

## Steps
1. Owner reopens #217.
2. Document semantic-core TIR laws in `docs/spec/tir.md` pointing at the Rust types as canon.
3. Restate R12 per D-ONECORE1=A in that doc.
4. Strengthen compile-time exhaustive coverage (interpreter mandatory; tier-1 via transparent deopt where applicable).
5. Differential tests: same TIR → identical observable semantics across lenses for the frozen subset.
6. Independent review; meet reopen + doc + test criteria.

## Acceptance / proof
Card criteria (reopen gate, tir.md laws, exhaustive consumer enforcement). Proof: tests fail if a node is added without all consumers.

## Blockers
blockedBy: #217. Semantic-core prerequisite #776 is already incorporated via D-ONECORE1=A (card retired); do not re-block on a missing id.

cards.title: Jet-in-Jet front-end milestone 1: lexer port + C-ABI link-in
cards.body: First concrete port milestone after owner-frozen #217 reopens and the architecture/behavioral prerequisites land. Port the current lexer contract to Jet, add one narrow internal integration ABI to the Rust driver, prove exact token/span/diagnostic parity, then replace the Rust path. This ABI is new internal bootstrap machinery, not a ratified user FFI surface or public compatibility promise. Driver orchestration owns query caching and module fan-out; the lexer stays one sequential implementation.
cards.plan:
## Goal
First Jet-in-Jet front-end milestone: port the public lexer contract to Jet, add the smallest internal C ABI for the Rust driver, prove token/span/diagnostic parity, then make the Jet path authoritative.

## Law
- Exact port of current public lexer contract (`lex`, `lex_raw`, TokKind/Token/StrTokPart, byte spans, interpolation, nested comments, terminator insertion, recovery, Jet-owned diagnostics).
- Use existing Syntax constants — no second keyword table (I7).
- ABI is internal only: owned buffers, token/diagnostic serialization, panic containment, alloc/free ownership, version lock; no user-facing export.
- One selectable comparison seam until parity; then Jet path authoritative with no facade.
- Driver owns jet-queries and fan-out; no lexer-local parallelism invention.

## Scope
In: Jet lexer sources; internal ABI; differential corpus + seeded fuzz vs Rust lexer; cutover.
Out: parser/sema ports (#809/#810); umbrella inventory (#218) except consuming its seam list.

## Owned paths
- new Jet lexer tree (location TBD under self-host layout from #218 inventory)
- `crates/jet-lexer` comparison seam / ABI bridge
- `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs` (consume, do not fork)
- fuzz/differential harnesses
- diagnostics remain I4-compliant (no new user codes unless behavior differs — should not)

## Steps
1. Gates: #217 reopened; #669 and #670 complete.
2. Port lexer to Jet against Syntax constants.
3. Specify and implement minimal internal C ABI; contain panics; lock versions.
4. Selectable seam: Rust vs Jet lexer; corpus + seeded fuzz differentials.
5. On parity, switch driver to Jet path; remove facade.
6. File only concrete next-port gaps; independent review.

## Acceptance / proof

criteria.text: A source ledger separates transcript claims, linked-author corrections, repeated comment corroboration, disputed anecdotes, and Jet-specific inference; every recommendation names its canonical owner or uncovered gap.

log.text:
CORRECTION to my earlier verification of criterion 2, and #688 cannot close yet.

I verified criterion 2 on the tripwire and the named deopt reasons. Both of those hold. I did not test the rest of the criterion text, the clause requiring deopt to produce identical observable behavior. That clause fails.

Measured at c485d5f17 with a fresh build. examples/features/crypto/crypto_suite.jet exits 0 under jet run --release and exits 1 under default jet run. examples/features/types/generic_constructor_inference.jet does the same; AOT prints '7 jet 2 9' and JIT prints an error. Both are byte-different, which is the exact condition this card exists to eliminate.

Mechanism: --trace-tiers confirms the deopt happens as designed ('run tier0 interp (body stmt 6: Let[0] init=OtherExpr)'). The problem is the target. Tier-0 is the comptime evaluator, and its own E0956 text says it evaluates a pure subset of Jet. So the deopt target cannot run what Cranelift could not compile.

This means the compile-gap ratchet drift the JIT worker reported is not manifest bookkeeping. Each entry is a real lens violation. Growing tests/jit_gaps.txt to absorb them would have recorded two parity failures as normal, so the worker was right to stop and ask.

Carded as #1254 and this card now blocks on it. Criteria 2 and 3 must be re-proved after #1254 lands. The JIT worker's tier-1 additions at c485d5f17 are correct and stay: sha512_bytes and blake3_bytes now compile resident and match AOT byte for byte.

STOP AND REPORT on the gap ratchet, as instructed. The gap set cannot return to zero inside this card, and I did not grow tests/jit_gaps.txt. Fresh JET_DUMP_JIT_GAPS=1 jit_coverage_audit at c485d5f17 shows covered 371 against a manifest of 370, and two gaps against a manifest of none. Gap one: 'crypto/crypto_suite: run: jit core call unsupported: jet.crypto.hkdf_sha256'. Behind it sit at least constant_time_equal, constant_time_equal_bytes, x25519_shared and file_seal, plus the Secret.from_bytes, X25519SecretKey.new_random, public_key and text method calls, none of which the JIT host table carries. Gap two: 'types/generic_constructor_inference: run: jit string interp type unsupported: Named("T")'. That one needs the lowerer to resolve a generic field type through monomorphisation before it can print it, which no host shim can supply. Gap two alone puts a zero gap set out of reach whatever I do to crypto. All three movements come from other workers' frontend fixes landing today and admitting three previously rejected examples into the compile attempt: crypto_suite from #1210, plus generic_constructor_inference and generic_modules. Criterion #3 assigns Cranelift completeness to the #778 ratchet and excludes it here. Card #771's example is not landed: its precondition, an empty gap set, is unmet, and it would add a third gap.

JIT hash coverage landed at c485d5f17: jet.crypto.sha512_bytes and jet.crypto.blake3_bytes now compile. A core call needs an entry in two tables, and both were missing: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs picks the Cranelift host function, and crates/jet-jit/src/jit/safety.rs decides whether the function stays resident. With only the lowering entry the planner still deopted the whole program before lowering ran, and tier-0 then refused the call with E0956. Both host shims reuse the shared jet_crypto_sha512_impl and jet_crypto_blake3_impl that the AOT bridge uses, so there is no second algorithm copy. A program printing both digests now reports 'run tier1 native' and matches jet run --release byte for byte. Three-way differential stays green for crypto/hash and crypto/typed_crypto. The gap ratchet is still red for two reasons that belong to other work; details in the next log.

Orchestrator verification at HEAD: criteria 2 and 4 verified independently. Criterion 3 is NOT verified — the compile-gap ratchet is red again. 'cargo test --test dev jit_try_compile_manifest_matches' fails at tests/dev.rs:6690 with drift ['crypto/crypto_suite: run: jit core call unsupported: jet.crypto.sha512_bytes'] against an expected empty set. Cause traced: commit 33873fcf4 (card #1210) repaired crypto.constant_time_eq, whose registered item pointed at a codegen target that did not exist. With that call fixed, crypto_suite.jet compiles further than before and reaches the next unsupported core call. This is a pre-existing JIT coverage hole that an earlier failure was masking, not a regression in 33873fcf4. Fix is assigned back to the JIT worker: give jet.crypto.sha512_bytes a core-call handler reusing the existing runtime implementation. tests/jit_gaps.txt must not grow; the ratchet is shrink-only.

Criteria 2, 3 and 4 met from fresh runs; card moves to verify for an independent check. One item stays open and belongs to card #771, not here: examples/features/io/process_terminal.jet is still untracked, is in neither tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt nor tests/jit_gaps.txt, and carries a real Cranelift gap, 'run: jit handle method unsupported'. Adding it grows the shrink-only gap ratchet from 0 to 1, which is card #771's call to make, so this agent left both manifests alone. Until #771 commits the example with its two ratchet entries, a local gate run in a dirty tree fails on that file alone, while a CI checkout stays green.

Persist migration committed at a5e21ff9d: examples/features/devloop/persist.jet, tests/dev.rs, tests/fuzz/sema/differential/ex_devloop_persist.jet, Source/JitBackend.rs. Targeted proof, all green: cargo test --test dev persist_ (2 passed, both were red before), cargo test --test dev jit_try_compile_manifest_matches (passed), JET_CORPUS_GATE_FILTER=devloop/ corpus gate (3 classified, 3 resident JIT), SEMA_SOUNDNESS_CASE=tests/fuzz/sema/differential/ex_devloop_persist.jet executable_corpus_matches_aot_and_default_dev (passed), JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=devloop/persist golden (passed), jet fmt --check on the example (clean). Gate was RED on master, not green. The full differential gate at 648800cf9 failed twice: example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate and jit_try_compile_manifest_matches, both exit 101. cards.title: XML: complete parser, renderer, and canonicalization
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 4. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: After D-ENCXML-PROJECTION1 is ratified, implement only the selected public surface. If A wins, add xml.decode<T>, xml.decode_bytes<T>, root(document), expanded_name(node) returning the typed name view, attribute(element, name) returning the normalized String value, and content(element) returning ordered DataTree nodes, with the ballot signatures and namespace rules. If B wins, add the same decode entry points and tree-native helpers that return the exact XMLName and attribute DataTree nodes. If C wins, add the same decode entry points and Clark-string name and normalized-value attribute helpers. For every verdict, wire parser -> DataTree projection -> Codable through foundation, comptime, sema, and codegen; preserve source locations for parse errors; report projection failures as XMLError.Shape without a source location and with the deepest projected path; select attributes by local or Clark name, never prefix; cover scalar $text and struct @, child, $text, and $content mappings; add executable examples, goldens, targeted tests, and an independent review. Then resume the ungated XML conformance slices: official XML/Namespaces parser corpora, licensed C14N 1.1 and Exclusive 1.0 vectors, dual-limit and allocator matrices, byte identity, token editing, and fold/unfold hostile cases. Do not edit dirty sema, diagnostic, core_calls, docs-reference, or crypto paths until ownership clears.

cards.title: Encoding: hostile streaming laws for non-XML codecs
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 5. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Resume by adding one production-faithful std-only hostile I/O seam shared by FileReader and FileWriter tests, without changing the public Jet surface. It must inject one-byte reads, short writes, Interrupted retries, failure after N bytes, and close/drop observation into the exact codec engines. Run the same matrix over JSON, JSONL, CSV, and CBOR, then retain existing real-file and /dev/full probes. Prove terminal clones, accepted-prefix bytes, no duplicate writes, no background work, allocator ceilings, and whole hostile corpora. Do not use generated-source substitution or a test-only codec implementation.

criteria.text: JSON, JSONL, CSV, and CBOR readers consume only enough wire input to return one event or record, preserve chunk-at-every-byte results, and enforce EncodingLimits before retaining bytes or allocating past the ratified live-heap ceiling.
criteria.evidence: Orch independent: encoding_hostile_io green in jet-bd-711 (verify-711.log). Reviewed ab20b886: env-gated EncodingHostileIo seam + matrix over JSON/JSONL/CSV/CBOR.

criteria.text: Writers apply synchronous blocking backpressure, reject an invalid event or record before accepting or emitting its bytes, handle short or interrupted writes without duplication, expose real partial-I/O failures, and never hide a queue, thread, callback, or partial-success state.
criteria.evidence: Orch independent: encoding_hostile_io green in jet-bd-711 (verify-711.log). Reviewed ab20b886: env-gated EncodingHostileIo seam + matrix over JSON/JSONL/CSV/CBOR.

criteria.text: Clean EOF appears only after complete structure and trailing-input checks; the first terminal read, write, flush, finish, state, limit, or IO error is latched and every later method returns an equal clone; successful finish is required and idempotent, while Drop only closes and never claims success.
criteria.evidence: Orch independent: encoding_hostile_io green in jet-bd-711 (verify-711.log). Reviewed ab20b886: env-gated EncodingHostileIo seam + matrix over JSON/JSONL/CSV/CBOR.

criteria.text: Hostile matrices cover every input byte boundary, malformed and truncated structures, duplicates, invalid UTF-8, non-finite or unsupported values, CBOR tags and key forms, JSONL record boundaries, CSV quoting and CRLF edges, canonical violations, typed decode failures, and prohibited permissive normalization.
criteria.evidence: Orch independent: encoding_hostile_io green in jet-bd-711 (verify-711.log). Reviewed ab20b886: env-gated EncodingHostileIo seam + matrix over JSON/JSONL/CSV/CBOR.

criteria.text: Counting-allocator and prospective-counter oracles prove buffer_bytes, max_depth, max_item_bytes, max_total_bytes, and codec-specific CBOR workspace bounds at legal endpoints and one-byte crossings without overflow, truncation, post-error growth, or caller-owned-value mischarging.
criteria.evidence: Orch independent: encoding_hostile_io green in jet-bd-711 (verify-711.log). Reviewed ab20b886: env-gated EncodingHostileIo seam + matrix over JSON/JSONL/CSV/CBOR.

criteria.text: Cancellation by scope exit or dropped handles closes consumed files without leaks, emits no false success, preserves bytes from earlier accepted items only, and leaves no resumable hidden operation or orphaned background work.
criteria.evidence: Orch independent: encoding_hostile_io green in jet-bd-711 (verify-711.log). Reviewed ab20b886: env-gated EncodingHostileIo seam + matrix over JSON/JSONL/CSV/CBOR.

cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 6. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.

Then implement D-JSONCANON1 RFC 8785 plus its 2026 boundary, D-ENCBASE-STRICT1 2027 strict parser on the existing shared 2026 engine, and CBOR 2026/2027/2028 compatibility entries. cards.title: Encoding: whole/stream and execution-tier parity
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 7. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Resume with one parity matrix instead of isolated format tests. First add a clean dedicated harness that records AOT, resident default-dev or transparent AOT fallback, and comptime outcomes. Cover pure whole-value codecs across all three tiers; cover file-backed streams in AOT and default-dev while asserting the named comptime ambient-I/O rejection. Then add per-format whole-versus-stream equivalence for values, bytes, errors, limits, terminal state, and file effects. Reuse production engines only; do not edit dirty core_calls.rs, fixed_sigs.rs, module_items.rs, or docs/reference/core-library.md.

criteria.text: Whole-value JSON, JSONL, CSV, XML, CBOR, base64, base64url, and base32 consumers produce byte-identical values, bytes, typed errors, paths, limits, and observable output in AOT, default-dev, and comptime wherever the operation is pure.

criteria.text: Collecting each valid stream reconstructs the structurally equal whole value, and unfolding a whole value yields the same accepted stream law; JSON canonical and CBOR deterministic modes use their one shared whole/stream serializer and byte law.
criteria.evidence: Orch: encoding_parity 8/8 in jet-bd-713 (verify-713.log). Reviewed 32a473c1f.

criteria.text: Comptime rejects file-backed readers and writers at the named ambient-I/O boundary while pure whole-value codecs remain available; tests distinguish this deliberate boundary from a missing implementation.
criteria.evidence: Orch: encoding_parity 8/8 in jet-bd-713 (verify-713.log). Reviewed 32a473c1f.

criteria.text: Every default-dev encoding probe records the backend path and proves any R12 AOT fallback is named, transparent, and behavior-preserving; no unsupported operation, fixture substitution, or silent engine switch can pass as resident parity.
criteria.evidence: Orch: encoding_parity 8/8 in jet-bd-713 (verify-713.log). Reviewed 32a473c1f.

criteria.text: Focused differential tests cover success, malformed input, typed decode, exact errors, limit endpoints, terminal repeats, and side effects across the applicable tiers, with no duplicate codec or test-only parity engine.

cards.title: Encoding: examples, corpora, docs, and diagnostics
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 8. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Resume after #710, #711, and #712 settle shipped behavior. cards.plan: Review starts only after every producer closes. #710 first resolves its open XML projection ballot and finishes XML. #711 hostile-stream and #712 edition-surface work can proceed in parallel. #713 then proves whole/stream and execution-tier parity on those final engines. #714 pins all official and hostile corpora, examples, goldens, docs, and diagnostics against the shipped behavior. #715 reviews the clean integrated range after #710 through #714 close; it does not repair producer code or certify partial work. Preserve earlier accepted checkpoints as scoped history, not final proof. Reviewer procedure: 1. Record authority, base and tip, producer identities, reviewer identity/model/effort, target facts, and clean status. Read the full integrated diff and map every #710-#714 criterion to implementation and test evidence. 2. Verify every corpus manifest before use. Check URL/version, license/notice, SHA-256, case count, transformation provenance, and test reachability. Separate published oracle vectors from local hostile cases. 3. Run published expected-value and byte vectors for JSON/JCS, CSV, XML/Namespaces/C14N, CBOR, and base encodings. Run an independent implementation for interoperable cases, record its exact version and command, and classify each variance by standard clause and selected profile. Product code gains no oracle dependency. 4. Trace tests to the production whole/stream engines, host I/O, allocator, terminal state, migration, tier, and diagnostic paths. Reject delimiter scanners, transcript comparison, generated-source substitution, fallback masking, and test-only codecs. 5. Run negative controls for omitted or changed corpus rows, bad hashes, wrong outputs, every hostile I/O fault, terminal-repeat drift, allocator and limit crossings, XML external access, migration drift, and backend substitution. Each control must make the named oracle red, then be removed. 6. Run every split up to 4096 bytes, 32 saved deterministic chunk plans above it, endpoint and overflow limits, and three clean repetitions per supported platform and tier. Preserve seeds, oracle/tool versions, outputs, first differences, and timings. 7. Report only concrete findings. Producers fix them. Reviewer rechecks material fixes, reruns exact affected proofs, then verifies #715 and parent #296 criterion 9 with commit-bound evidence.

cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #688 criterion 2. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #688 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Authority is D-VERDICT-687-1. Default jet run uses JIT. jet build and jet run --release use AOT. A JIT gap is a compiler defect, not a fallback. Current dispatch violates that law. Default jet run enters run_compile_cmd and builds native Rust. Default jet dev constructs CraneliftBackend over AotFallbackBackend over InterpreterBackend. Hot swap and restart use the same ladder. CraneliftBackend delegates on a missing program or any JIT compile error. AotFallbackBackend compiles and runs AOT, then uses the interpreter when AOT is unavailable. Interpreter.rs also reruns an E0953 JIT result through AOT. That retry can duplicate effects. Explicit jet dev --interpret correctly uses InterpreterBackend and E2201. No E2211 source, registry row, snapshot, explain entry, or CLI test exists. Use this exact diagnostic copy. What: Jet JIT has a compiler gap for this checked program. Why: jet run uses the JIT lens and does not hide a JIT compiler gap by running AOT. Fix: run jet build <file> and the binary for now, then report E2211 with the detail below. Detail: JIT gap in {function}: {reason}. Attach the entry function span when available. Keep raw Rust and rustc text hidden. Return exit 101 because the exit table defines compiler defects as ICE. A watching dev session prints E2211, keeps the last good state, and continues. One-shot dev and default run exit 101. --try-anyway applies only to interpreter E2201 and never bypasses E2211. Implement in one order. First change api_debug try_resident, hot_swap, and restart from Option to Result and preserve unsupported host, lowering, safety, compilation, and panic reasons. Then make CraneliftBackend strict and remove its fallback generic. Delete AotFallbackBackend and its native subprocess runner after all product callers move. Keep InterpreterBackend only for explicit --interpret. Remove the E0953 AOT retry. Route default run to the same strict Cranelift backend. Keep build and run --release on CmdCompile AOT. Update watch, restart, and swap so a failed edit retains the last good runtime. Register E2211 under the JIT diagnostics area. Add the exact what, why, and fix row. Update the stale dev-loop prose. Add a rendered tests/dev/jit_gap.txt snapshot and generated error reference. Test supported JIT run, each gap class, unsupported host, no duplicate effects, watch recovery, one-shot exit 101, JSON, color, NO_COLOR, explain, default run, build, release run, and explicit interpreter. Re-run the #727 strict corpus gate. Do not add a daemon, alternate runner, new cache, or runtime AOT fallback.

cards.title: JIT/AOT: enforce parity in CI
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #688 criterion 4. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #688 govern this slice.
cards.plan:
Amended 2026-07-24 after D-ONECORE1=A / D-LENS-RUN2=A. Prerequisites: #776-#778 replace the old #729-to-zero prerequisite; the gate ships with #778.
1. Restore the ratified D-CI3 triggers in .github/workflows/ci.yml (push, pull_request, nightly, workflow_dispatch); keep the full verify job.
2. Add one named parity job running #727's canonical command in three modes per case: pure-interpreter (tier 0), default tiered run, optimized AOT — byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit across all three. E2211 assertions are retired with #778.
3. tests/jit_gaps.txt is enforced as a shrink-only ratchet: additions need a named reason in the same reviewed diff; CI never rewrites it.
4. Native x86_64 and aarch64 runners for every host #729 proves; fail-fast false; 45-minute job limit; canonical reports uploaded with if: always() and 30-day retention.
5. Same strict job in release.yml; tag, test, and artifact commits must match.
6. Prove failure behavior with canaries (output mismatch, ratchet growth, timeout each make the job red), remove canaries, independent review, close.

cards.title: Script-speed run loop: cached re-run, jet dev signpost, start budget
cards.body:
Persona audit 2026-07-23: every `jet run` costs 12-14s, even when the file did not change. `jet dev` runs the same file in 4.7s, but `jet run` never mentions it. Python starts at once. The focused agent audit also measured an unchanged process example at 36.38s through the required development environment. This gap decides the script persona and blocks Jet from replacing Bash, Python, and Node for short agent tasks.

Work:
- An unchanged file re-runs from cache with no recompile.
- `jet run` prints one tip line when a compile is slow: point at `jet dev`.
- Measure and enforce cold/warm script budgets against matched Bash, Python, and Node tasks.

Rides #687/#688 (jet run = JIT lens) and #439 (watch engine). The self-host era work (#666/#669) is the long game; this card owns the Epoch 3 daily-driver feel.
cards.plan:
Amended 2026-07-24: two facts change this card. First, the 2026-07-24 environment fix (batch-pass rewrite of scripts/agent/clean-nix-tmp.sh) removed a multi-minute shellHook stall; the recorded no-op baseline (jet-env true 57.826 s, cold 13.905 s, warm 12.088 s) is invalid — re-measure all spans before enforcing any budget. Second, D-ONECORE1=A / D-LENS-RUN2=A (#776-#778) make default jet run tiered; the interpreter tier needs no Cranelift compile, which changes the cold-start calculus.
Resume when #778 lands the tiered run path and #439 exposes the shared invalidation service. Put warm artifact reuse at the tier boundary: cache compiled tier-1 modules keyed by exact source, dependency, compiler-build identity, target, capability, and configuration facts; a hit skips load, parse, check, lowering, and code generation with trace proof. Do not extend the AOT BuildCache path or add another runner, cache, watcher, or daemon. Measure spans separately: environment entry; compiler startup; load; parse; check; TIR lowering; tier-1 compile; artifact load; program time. Add the slow-run signpost only in the common run coordinator (once, stderr, TTY-aware, NO_COLOR/JSON suppressed). Benchmark matched no-op, file/JSON, and subprocess fixtures against Bash, Python, and Node; record machine facts, cold and warm medians, and tail latency; enforce the ratified budget only after the method and value exist.

cards.title: Exclusive range spelling for index loops
cards.body:

Ballot D-RANGE-EXCL1 on this card decides: add an exclusive spelling, bless Jet-native idioms (sequence two-binding + `indexes`, pipeline `indexed`), or both. S22 inclusive-by-default is not reopened. Rec C would also amend D-ITER1 `enumerate` → `indexed`.

Extend list and fixed-list source loops so two bindings receive index then item, while one binding remains item-only. Add the indexes sequence member through the existing builtin-member path and emit valid Int indexes only. In sema, recognize only the provable same-root shape where an inclusive loop ends at xs.len() and its body indexes xs; report a registered teaching diagnostic with the three ratified fixes and avoid heuristic lookalikes. Rename the public D-ITER1 adapter enumerate() to indexed() across sema, TIR, codegen, docs, examples, and tests, preserving the named tuple contract. cards.body:
Persona audit (Devon): `todo add "buy milk"` fails and demands `--text`. The builder API has `.positional(…)`; the `@Cli` derive does not. A Node dev tries the positional form first — this is the first thing they hit.

A derive-side spelling is new user-typeable marker surface (I7), so ballot D-CLI-POS1 on this card picks it. Implementation follows ratification.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-CLI-POS1=A through the existing #[Cli] derive and shared ArgsSpec/CliSchema parser. Register the current-plane #[Flag] field marker in the syntax registry. In sema, classify required value fields as positional by default in declaration order, while Boolean flags and optional/defaulted fields remain flag-only; retain every named --field spelling and define named input as the winner. Extend CliSchema with positional eligibility and order, then make codegen register the existing positional parser and decode named input before positional input. Keep validation and user diagnostics in sema. Propagate the shape to help, completions, schema/dossier output, and publish API diff. Add an executable example plus focused UI, golden, and AOT/dev parity coverage, then complete syntax regeneration, snapshots, and scoped verification.

Implementing D-CLI-POS1=A: #[Flag] marker, CliSchema positional order, ArgsSpec named-wins, derive codegen. Tower via main board.
started on burndown-e3-748 (parallel Cli positional; avoid TIR/jit paths)

Foreign-dirty tests/cli.rs blocks the natural integration tests. Existing reusable mechanism: jet_args_positional and jet_parsed_positional. Current behavior: RequiredOption emits only jet_args_option and decode reads only jet_parsed_option; CliInputShape has only Flag/Value.

Audit found a broad unshipped slice. The derive still maps required scalar fields only to required --options. #Flag is not registered. CliSchema metadata, dossier, completions, API snapshots, examples, and tests have no derive-position information. The current positional parser also requires every registered positional even when its named option exists, so named-wins needs a deliberate shared-parser change. tests/cli.rs is dirty under another task and stayed read-only.
Started audit against ratified D-CLI-POS1=A. Relevant source paths are clean; tests/cli.rs is dirty and remains read-only.

Reconciled against ratified D-CLI-POS1=A. The ballot predates the current marker plane, so implementation uses #[Cli] and #[Flag] while preserving the ratified semantics. Card is implementation-ready; no new owner decision is required.

cards.title: Browser debugging: source maps for the web target
cards.body:
Field audit TypeScript row: the browser is the runtime and feedback is live. Jet ships a web/canvas target, but devtools cannot step Jet lines.

Work: emit source maps for the JS/Wasm output so browser devtools show and step Jet source. The compiler already maps Jet lines to generated Rust for diagnostics (Source/Compiler.rs SourceMap) — extend that chain to the browser. Rides the web wave (#123, #701-#705).

Flip test: set a breakpoint on a Jet line in browser devtools and step.
cards.plan: 1. Reuse `TStmt::LineMarker` for web output. Do not add a second source-location model. 2. Add a std-only Source Map v3 encoder with stable source order. Use UTF-16 columns for JavaScript. 3. Record generated JavaScript positions before each emitted TIR statement. Emit `app.js.map` and its relative `sourceMappingURL`. 4. Compile Wasm with line data. Read rustc's Wasm line table after compilation. Join generated Rust lines to Jet lines through existing markers. 5. Emit Wasm byte-offset mappings in `app.wasm.map`. Put the relative map URL in the Wasm `sourceMappingURL` custom section. 6. Default, debug, and CI web builds include exact Jet bytes in `sourcesContent`. Release builds emit no maps or map references. 7. Use project-relative source names with `/` separators. Never emit absolute host paths. 8. Add both map files to build output, atomic dev swaps, static serving, and last-good rebuild behavior. 9. Reuse the current Chromium CDP harness. Prove Jet breakpoints and stepping in JavaScript and Wasm. 10. Run focused web tests and fresh review. If Wasm decoding needs a new tool or crate, stop and raise a dependency ballot.

cards.title: Data-race freedom: state it, prove it, test it
cards.body:
Field audit Go row: Go ships a race detector. Jet's answer should be stronger: the memory model plus structured concurrency may rule races out by construction (E1101 already rejects a var captured across tasks).

Work: state in the spec exactly what the model guarantees about data races, prove the claim over the concurrency surface (channels, task groups, parallel adapters), and lock it with adversarial tests. If a hole exists, raise the decision: static rule vs runtime detector.

Flip test: the docs can say "data races cannot compile" and a test suite backs it.

cards.title: Toolchain telemetry and trust policy
cards.body:
Lessons-learned gap 2 (2026-07-23): Go's telemetry episode and Audacity show that even well-intentioned opt-out telemetry burns trust permanently. Nothing on the board mentions telemetry — deciding it implicitly by code later is the expensive path.

Ballot D-TELEMETRY1 on this card decides: opt-in only vs none at all, and exactly what jet/jetpack may send over the network (registry queries included).
cards.plan:
Implement ratified D-TELEMETRY1=A and D-REPORT-SEND1=A only. No new owner choices.

1. Inventory every jet/jetpack network path. Prove builds and ordinary commands never open telemetry, crash, or usage endpoints.
2. Keep registry/package traffic limited to what the user-requested operation needs (name, version constraint, protocol necessities).
3. Ship or harden `jet report` as a local inspectable bundle writer that prints the path. Do not ship `jet report --send` (D-REPORT-SEND1 amends the illustrative telemetry example).
4. Document the permanent zero-telemetry promise in owner-facing tooling docs.
5. Add regression tests that fail if a background usage/crash sender appears, and CLI tests for local report bundle creation without network send.

Proof: focused CLI/tooling tests + greps/audit of network call sites. No full suite required for this card alone.

cards.title: #Persist: implement actual hot-reload value persistence in jet dev
cards.plan: Implement the already-ratified #Persist behavior at the shared runtime-heap boundary used by tier-0 and tier-1. cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#768:0] Split from the former #768 umbrella. This card owns only “MCP SDK: protocol types, negotiation, and lifecycle.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #768. The other 8 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
First MCP SDK slice under D-MCP-SURFACE1=A: protocol types, revision negotiation, and lifecycle over one protocol core. Typed builders for beginners; same engine for experts.

## Law (ratified)
- Layered typed SDK over one revisioned protocol core — not marker syntax, not low-level-only.
- Stable revisions negotiate by default; preview revisions need explicit policy until final.
- Per-revision codecs; `2025-11-25` session behavior; `2026-07-28` RC as separate codec when enabled.
- Bounded schema depth, message size, validation time, deadlines, redirects, origins, tokens, extension sets; audited.
- No token passthrough; unified grant graph; redacted traces; `jet inspect dossier` facts.
- Compiler seams stay dependency-free (I6); MCP lives in stdlib/tooling packages, not compiler crates.

## Scope
In: message/codec/peer lifecycle types; version policy; initialize/initialized (stable) and RC profile hooks; negotiation errors; audit facts for this slice.
Out: client convenience (#1061); server tools/resources/prompts (#1062); stdio (#1063); HTTP (#1064); OAuth (#1065); schema/reflection bridge (#1066); interop examples (#1067); hostile proof (#1068).

## Owned paths
- new `core.mcp` (or ratified package path) protocol modules
- docs/reference/core-library.md MCP section (protocol slice only)
- focused protocol/negotiation tests
- dossier fact keys for version negotiation and lifecycle

## Steps
1. Add revision registry + codecs for stable `2025-11-25`; stub/gate RC `2026-07-28` behind explicit policy.
2. Public types: messages, capabilities, peer lifecycle, `McpPolicy` version field.
3. Negotiation: stable-by-default; preview opt-in; downgrade refusal with clear error.
4. Emit grant/dossier facts for negotiated version and lifecycle stage.
5. Tests: success, incompatible peer, preview without opt-in, bounds.
6. Leave transports and tool registration to sibling cards; independent review.

## Acceptance / proof
Criteria 1–3 for this slice only. Proof: protocol unit/integration tests; no transport false-green.

cards.title: Agent executor: authority and resource policy model
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #770 umbrella. This card owns only: Agent executor: authority and resource policy model. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Give Jet programs and AI agents one safe way to execute untrusted commands. The beginner default grants only declared workspace reads/writes and no network or secrets. Experts can grant exact capabilities and receive a complete plan and receipt. This is the application-facing consumer of #398's native Linux/macOS/Windows isolation boundary, not a second sandbox engine. It extends the shipped #291 core.process model instead of adding a shell DSL or parallel process API.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-AGENT-EXEC1=A: one `ProcessAuthority` model on `core.process` with safe workspace defaults, exact expert grants, dry-run plans, and redacted receipts. Application-facing consumer of #398/#893 native isolation — not a second sandbox.

## Law (ratified)
- Extend `ProcessSpec` / `ProcessChild`; no parallel agent executor or shell DSL.
- Workspace constructor: useful read-only repo + private build writes; deny network, home, secrets, devices, inherited handles by default.
- Experts widen exact rights on the same object (write paths, hosts, secrets, executables, limits).
- Resolve executable identity before review; bind identity + policy + inputs + backend into one launch transaction.
- Plan and receipt share a policy digest; unsupported enforcement fails closed before spawn.
- CLI (`jet self exec --workspace …`) and MCP tools use the same engine.
- Integrate D-WD1 grant graph and D-WD2 dossier facts for denied attempts, descendants, limits, outputs, redaction.

## Scope
In: `ProcessAuthority` API, workspace defaults, plan/receipt, CLI parity, grant/dossier wiring, hostile tests once #893 corpus is available.
Out: building the isolation engine itself (#398 family); MCP protocol SDK (#768+); interactive terminal naming (#771 / D-PROCESS-SESSION2).

## Owned paths
- process corelib + jetpack runtime policy seams referenced on the card
- CLI exec surface
- hostile corpus consumption from #893 / #398
- docs/reference/core-library.md, architecture notes, diagnostics as needed
- focused success/failure/hostile/integration tests

## Steps
1. Confirm #398 engine + #893 shared hostile corpus are the only enforcement backends; fail closed when a grant cannot be enforced on the host.
2. Add `ProcessAuthority.workspace` and exact grant builders on `ProcessSpec.under(policy)`.
3. Implement dry-run `plan()` and final receipt with shared digest; redact secrets.
4. Wire denied-attempt and tree facts into the existing grant/dossier path.
5. CLI parity for workspace and expert grants.
6. Hostile tests: ambient authority denied; TOCTOU bind; full-tree cleanup; API/CLI parity.
7. Independent review against criteria.

## Acceptance / proof
Existing criteria 1–3. Proof: focused process/authority tests + hostile corpus cases; dossier facts visible via `jet inspect` where applicable.

## Blockers
blockedBy: #893 (and through it the #398 isolation delivery). D-AGENT-EXEC1 ratified (=A) — decision id kept for audit trail only; it does not block.

Add terminal-backed child sessions, binary streams, process-tree control, and resource limits without creating a second process API or a shell parser. Non-interactive argv execution remains the safe default; terminal semantics are explicit opt-in. Planning must ballot any new public Core type or function name before code.
cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
D-PROCESS-SESSION1 must choose the public extension to ProcessSpec and ProcessChild. Keep non-interactive argv execution as the safe default. Use native Unix PTYs and Windows ConPTY, with one byte-stream and lifecycle model. Make interrupt, terminate, kill, wait, timeout, and drop control the full process tree. Reuse core.io, core.watcher, core.event, task cancellation, and native job or process-group controls. Add no terminal emulator or sibling process module.

cards.body:

cards.title: One canonical interpreter over the semantic TIR core
cards.body:
Today Jet has three separate answers to "what does this program do": the AOT Rust emitter, the Cranelift JIT lowering, and the comptime tree-walker that also serves jet dev --interpret and the REPL. Each has its own coverage holes and its own bug surface.

This card builds one interpreter that walks the semantic TIR core from #776 and makes it the reference for runtime behavior. Comptime, the REPL, jet dev --interpret, and the deopt tier of jet run (card below) all execute through it. The AST tree-walker in jet-comptime retires for those roles.

Payoff: a new feature is executable the day its TIR lowering lands, because the interpreter's exhaustive match forces coverage at compile time of the compiler itself. The comptime-parity work on cards #392/#721/#722/#723 feeds this directly; their builtin inventory becomes the interpreter's host surface.
cards.plan:
1. Build a TIR evaluator (values, places, calls, control flow) with an exhaustive, wildcard-free match over executable TIR — a new variant fails the compiler build until the interpreter handles it.
2. Port the comptime builtin/host surface (the inventory from card #721) onto it.
3. Route jet dev --interpret, the REPL, and comptime block evaluation through the one evaluator. Keep comptime purity rules (E0951/E0956) as a policy layer on top, not a separate engine.
4. Retire the AST tree-walker paths in Source/Interpreter.rs and jet-comptime that the evaluator replaces.
5. Prove semantic parity: run the full AOT-runnable example corpus (from the #727 differential gate) under the interpreter; stdout, stderr, and exit codes must match the compiled binary.

Acceptance: one evaluator serves comptime, REPL, and dev interpret; corpus differential green; the retired walker paths are deleted, not parked.
Owned paths: crates/jet-comptime/**, Source/Interpreter.rs, Source/JitBackend.rs, new evaluator module beside TIR, touched tests.

cards.title: Bare bindings: retire the typed binding forms
cards.body: Binding grammar collapses to name :: value, name := value, name = value. The forms name: Type :: expr and name: Type := expr are removed as an immediate clean break — ordinary parse error, no teaching/retirement window. Types ride the value (Type.{ } heads, .new/.from_* calls); names carry types only in signatures and fields. Corpus migration: ~206 typed bindings rewrite mechanically.
cards.plan:
blockedBy: none

Authority: D-BIND-BARE1=A (ratified). Amends S1 / D-BIND4. Prerequisite feature: #780 universal Type.{ } heads (D-DOTCTOR3 shipped).

Goal: A binding is always bare. Keep only name :: value, name := value, and reassignment name = value. Delete name: Type :: expr and name: Type := expr. Immediate clean break — ordinary parse error, no teaching window.

## 1. Syntax authority
- Add the D-BIND-BARE1 entry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs.
- Append the syntax-decisions.md log: bindings never carry types; types ride values or live on signatures and fields.
- Run jet devtools grammars.
- Update Source/LSP/Completion.rs snippets that still teach typed bindings.

## 2. Parser
Owned: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/bindings.rs (and formatter Statements.rs).
- Remove the typed :: and := binding productions.
- Keep name: Type on signatures, struct fields, and other non-binding positions.
- Old typed bindings become an ordinary parse error — no special retirement diagnostic.
- Formatter never emits typed binding forms.
- Editor grammars match the parser.

## 3. Sema
- Local bindings stop carrying a required annotation for emptiness, sized numbers, and similar cases; the value head from #780 supplies the type.
- Signatures and fields keep name: Type.
- Sweep binding helpers that assume Binding.ty is present for ordinary locals.

## 4. Corpus migration (~206)
- Mechanical rewrite: drop a redundant annotation when the value already self-types; otherwise lift the annotation’s type onto the value as a Type.{ } head or assertion.
- Touch examples/, tests/, and Jet sources under std as needed.
- Update docs/spec/spec.md binding bullets that still list typed forms.

## 5. Lowering / TIR
- No new runtime for bare bindings already supported.
- Confirm destructuring and other binding variants still parse after the grammar cut.

## 6. Diagnostics / UI snapshots (I4)
- Snapshot the ordinary parse error for retired typed forms.
- Re-bless any UI snapshots whose fix text still shows name: Type :: / :=.
- Hand uninit trigger changes to #782; do not leave a typed-binding-only uninit path.

## 7. Acceptance tests
- Corpus grep: zero live name: Type :: / name: Type := forms in .jet sources (comments that teach the retirement are fine).
- Example goldens and formatter round-trips green.
- scripts/agent/jet-env scoped tests + jet run on touched examples.

Implement after #780. Prefer one delivery stream: heads first, then this cut.

cards.body: The one batch-boundary run of scripts/agent/verify-full.sh stopped in jet lib tests. Focused LSP proofs pass when RUST_MIN_STACK=16 MiB, so the default full-suite path is not robust. This red is outside closed #751/#794/#795 behavior.

Keep the full suite usable without a global RUST_MIN_STACK crutch. If the test harness itself owns the large frame, isolate it with a joined bounded-stack wrapper that propagates panic. Add a nearby completion regression and run the full LSP library before one later full-suite closeout.

cards.title: Unified FFI: ownership, error, and layout conversion
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #180 umbrella. This card owns only: Unified FFI: ownership, error, and layout conversion. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Owner directive (2026-07-02): reopen FFI structure with the bar set at revolutionary UX/DX — it should be almost trivial to use almost any other language as a wrapper/binding, so in-situ replacements are easy and Jet can tap ALL developments of other ecosystems immediately. This ballot picks the shared architecture (surface law); per-language depth (binder strategy for Python, JS, Swift, …) follows as one ballot each on that frame. Existing ratifications are inputs, not casualties: S50 (extern rust), S59 (C namespaces + bindgen/overlay — already the C instance of the recommended shape), D-NPMTYPE1 (typed npm stubs), D-JSWIFTFFI1 (JS first, Swift via C-ABI later). Ballot D-FFI-UNIFY1 attached.
cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
Use D-FFI-UNIFY1=A as one foreign-namespace architecture: generated typed stubs and binders feed a common checked FFI boundary, while each language adapter owns transport details. Finish canonical descriptor, ownership/error/layout conversion, safe-vs-#Unsafe boundary, build/cache/provenance, package provider integration, and per-language capability reporting. Reconcile Python A, external provider A, existing C/Rust/npm/JS/Swift law, and active polyglot phase cards. Keep compiler seams dependency-free; foreign dependencies live in generated bridge/runtime packages.

Single-task slice extracted from former #180 umbrella. This card owns only: Unified FFI: bridge builds, cache identity, and provenance. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Owner directive (2026-07-02): reopen FFI structure with the bar set at revolutionary UX/DX — it should be almost trivial to use almost any other language as a wrapper/binding, so in-situ replacements are easy and Jet can tap ALL developments of other ecosystems immediately. This ballot picks the shared architecture (surface law); per-language depth (binder strategy for Python, JS, Swift, …) follows as one ballot each on that frame. Existing ratifications are inputs, not casualties: S50 (extern rust), S59 (C namespaces + bindgen/overlay — already the C instance of the recommended shape), D-NPMTYPE1 (typed npm stubs), D-JSWIFTFFI1 (JS first, Swift via C-ABI later). Ballot D-FFI-UNIFY1 attached.
cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
Use D-FFI-UNIFY1=A as one foreign-namespace architecture: generated typed stubs and binders feed a common checked FFI boundary, while each language adapter owns transport details. Finish canonical descriptor, ownership/error/layout conversion, safe-vs-#Unsafe boundary, build/cache/provenance, package provider integration, and per-language capability reporting. Reconcile Python A, external provider A, existing C/Rust/npm/JS/Swift law, and active polyglot phase cards. Keep compiler seams dependency-free; foreign dependencies live in generated bridge/runtime packages.

log.text: R-E3-1: split from #180 as one effort-sized task (5/8).

criteria.text: Unified FFI: bridge builds, cache identity, and provenance works end to end through the existing production path.

Documentation and audit evidence match Unified FFI: bridge builds, cache identity, and provenance, and an independent reviewer verifies the result.

cards.title: core.compute: ndarray operations, broadcasting, ufuncs, and fusion
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #443 umbrella. This card owns only: core.compute: ndarray operations, broadcasting, ufuncs, and fusion. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Complete typed ndarray/table foundations, broadcasting, ufuncs, linalg, FFT, sparse data, autodiff, training/inference, serialization, and a native accelerator model across CPU SIMD, CUDA, Metal, and Vulkan/WebGPU. Reuse existing array/View/Vec/Matrix, ownership, Gpu effect, and #Unsafe law; gpu.* providers remain compatibility bridges. Owner decisions select the canonical public model, type/shape relation, placement/fallback, kernel safety, autodiff, and backend contract before implementation.
cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
Implement all D-COMPUTE*=D outcomes as one core.compute operation family over an expert buffer/device/stream/kernel substrate. Tensor<T> is the owner; unified provenance-aware views and Vec/Matrix aliases share storage. Auto placement emits receipts; policy may narrow only. Safe kernels require sema proof; raw kernels stay @Unsafe/#Unsafe with typed contracts. Reverse autodiff defaults with jvp/vjp and definition-site rules. Portable precision/determinism profiles use CPU oracle differential tests; dev/AOT backend identity cannot drift. Integrate data/ML without a second graph or type system.

cards.title: Agent executor: dry-run plan
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #770 umbrella. This card owns only: Agent executor: dry-run plan. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Give Jet programs and AI agents one safe way to execute untrusted commands. The beginner default grants only declared workspace reads/writes and no network or secrets. Experts can grant exact capabilities and receive a complete plan and receipt. This is the application-facing consumer of #398's native Linux/macOS/Windows isolation boundary, not a second sandbox engine. It extends the shipped #291 core.process model instead of adding a shell DSL or parallel process API.
cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
D-AGENT-EXEC1 must choose the API and CLI spelling. Extend core.process and consume #398's native isolation engine. Keep argv execution canonical. The policy must deny ambient authority, describe exact grants, and produce one dry-run plan plus one final receipt. After ratification, block implementation on #398 and reuse its Linux, macOS, and Windows hostile proof. Add no second sandbox, process API, shell DSL, or container fallback.

cards.title: Process sessions: Unix PTY backend
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #771 umbrella. This card owns only: Process sessions: Unix PTY backend. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Complete the shipped #291 core.process model for interactive agent and developer tools. Add terminal-backed child sessions, binary streams, process-tree control, and resource limits without creating a second process API or a shell parser. Non-interactive argv execution remains the safe default; terminal semantics are explicit opt-in. Planning must ballot any new public Core type or function name before code.
cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
D-PROCESS-SESSION1 must choose the public extension to ProcessSpec and ProcessChild. Keep non-interactive argv execution as the safe default. Use native Unix PTYs and Windows ConPTY, with one byte-stream and lifecycle model. Make interrupt, terminate, kill, wait, timeout, and drop control the full process tree. Reuse core.io, core.watcher, core.event, task cancellation, and native job or process-group controls. Add no terminal emulator or sibling process module.

cards.body: Rust can return a borrow chosen from several inputs. It can also store borrows in lists, tuples, sums, closures, and trait-backed APIs. Jet requires one stable source for each output slot. It rejects these safe forms with E2305 or E2307.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close field-audit G1 under D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A: keep `View<T>` unchanged, and let sema track a bounded set of possible owners for each live view.

## Law (ratified)
- Public source stays free of lifetime syntax.
- Sema records a bounded owner-path union per view slot.
- Every possible owner stays live while the view is live.
- Lists, tuples, options, results, enums, callbacks, and trait values carry the same hidden relation.
- API metadata publishes the union; breaking provenance changes are visible in public API snapshots.

## Scope
In: provenance algebra in sema; return/store/callback/trait paths; API facts; examples and tests for multi-owner returns and aggregates.
Out: disjoint mutable proofs (#1198), taskgroup borrows (#1199), pin (#1200), Cell/Shared polish (#1201/#1202).

## Owned paths
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs`
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/lambdas.rs`
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs`
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerItems.rs`
- public API / dossier fact emission for source unions
- `tests/ownership.rs`
- `examples/features/memory/returned_views.jet` (extend) plus a zero-copy multi-buffer parser example
- `docs/spec/spec.md` provenance section; audit cross-links

## Steps
1. Model `SourceSet` / owner-union on tracked views; keep single-owner as the common case.
2. Allow return and rebinding when every path's owner is in the declared or inferred union.
3. Carry unions through aggregates (list/tuple/option/result/enum fields) and through function values / lambdas / trait dispatch contracts.
4. Publish API facts (`one_of(owners…)`) and fail closed on incompatible dynamic dispatch.
5. Keep E2305/E2307 for true escapes; retarget wording where a union is legal.
6. Golden + ownership tests for `longer`, tokenize-across-two-buffers, aggregate-carried views, and trait-backed lending APIs.
7. Independent review against criteria; no owner ballot remains.

## Acceptance / proof
Meet card criteria 1–5. Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ownership` plus new focused cases; example goldens; API snapshot diffs that show provenance unions.

## Blockers
blockedBy: none. D-MEMPROVENANCE2 ratified (=A). Prefer landing after or with #1196 checker unification if overlapping place paths are still open.

criteria.text: A safe function can return a view chosen at runtime from compatible input owners.
Lists, tuples, options, results, enums, and named aggregates can carry proven read or write views.
Function values, lambdas, generic callbacks, and trait dispatch preserve returned-view provenance without unsafe code.
Public API snapshots record source relations and report breaking provenance changes.
Zero-copy parser and borrowing-deserializer examples work without copies, raw pointers, or user-written lifetime syntax.

cards.title: View parity: runtime-proven disjoint mutable access
cards.body: Rust safe APIs can split a slice at a runtime index and borrow several distinct map entries. Jet proves only static fields, indices, and ranges. Dynamic projections stay overlapping, so safe mutable iterators and multi-index edits have no general form.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close field-audit G2 under D-MEMDISJOINT1=A: one checked disjointness proof with beginner `edit_disjoint`, expert `get_disjoint_write` / `split_write`, and lending mutable iteration.

## Law (ratified)
- Ordinary range syntax stays compile-time only; never hide runtime overlap failure in bare loans.
- All forms lower to one sema-visible proof for one owner.
- Normalize regions and finish every bounds/duplicate/overlap check before any view is created.
- Explicit forms return tracked `ViewMut` under existing loan rules.
- One typed bounds-or-overlap error family.

## Scope
In: slice split, multi-index/key disjoint APIs, lending mutable iterators, JIT/dev/AOT parity.
Out: multi-owner provenance (#1197) except consuming its aggregate-view ability; taskgroup (#1199); pin/Cell/Shared.

## Owned paths
- ownership checker + corelib method lowering for collections/slices
- codegen/TIR paths that mint multiple `ViewMut`s
- `tests/ownership.rs` and differential cases vs Rust `split_at_mut` / `get_disjoint_mut`
- examples under `examples/features/memory/`
- docs for the three entry points (teach closure first)

## Steps
1. Add runtime region normalization + pairwise overlap/duplicate checks as one proof helper.
2. Ship `split_write(mid)` (one bounds check → two views).
3. Ship `edit_disjoint(targets, closure)` as beginner default; auto-release loans on all exits.
4. Ship `get_disjoint_write` for views that cross helpers.
5. Extend lending mutable iteration to one exclusive element loan at a time.
6. Reject overlap before mutation; shared error type; identical behavior across JIT/dev/AOT.
7. Differential tests against Rust class programs; independent review.

## Acceptance / proof
Criteria 1–5. Proof: ownership + concurrency tests; runtime overlap/duplicate cases; example that updates two physics bodies by index.

## Blockers
blockedBy: none. D-MEMDISJOINT1 ratified (=A). Natural dependency: #1197 if disjoint results must live in tuples/lists.
