options.detail: Canvas re-runs the program on the tier-0 interpreter with instrumentation and animates a deterministic, smooth exec pulse plus interpreter-computed watch values. No native process is involved. Visually the richest and most controllable, but the values and path are the interpreter's, which can differ from the compiled program.
options.code:
Dana clicks Run:

  [ interpreter overlay ]
  Watches:   total = 4299   (interpreter's evaluation)
  Exec pulse: smooth flowing highlight along price -> if -> charge

Risk made concrete: if `price(cart)` reads a clock, hits the network, or
depends on evaluation order, the interpreter's `total` and chosen path may
not match what the shipped binary does — the glow would show a run that
did not happen. Honest only if labeled "simulated preview," not "debug."

options.name: Hybrid (native state + interpreter pulse)
options.detail: A native session provides real variable/stack/step state; the exec-wire pulse animation is driven by the interpreter overlay for smoothness. State is real, motion is simulated.
options.code:
Dana clicks Run:

  Watches:   total = 4299            (real, from native session)
  Call stack: checkout <- main       (real)
  Exec pulse: smooth flow price->if->charge   (interpreter-animated)

The numbers are true but the flowing highlight is the interpreter's guess;
if the two disagree on the taken branch, the UI shows real values under a
pulse tracing a different path — a truthful-looking screen that lies in motion.

options.name: Debug the running tier: native session for compiled runs, in-tier session under jet dev (hybrid, recommended)
options.detail: One debugger UX behind one seam, backend chosen by what is actually executing. Compiled target: the existing jet debug lldb/DAP backend — option A verbatim, real process, real frames mapped by the existing source map. Under jet dev: the tier-0/tier-1 engine that IS running the program reports its own stops, values, and taken path — real liveness because it is the runtime, guaranteed behavior-identical by R12/D-DEVMODE1 and pinned by the existing parity batteries, which the debug facts join. The engine is always named on screen; no session, no pulse, ever. Breakpoints/watches stay local span-anchored state (D-CANVAS-DEBUGSTATE1) and drive both backends identically.
options.code:
Dana under `jet dev` (the beginner default), breakpoint on `charge`:

  [ debugging: dev tier — paused at charge ]
  Watches:    total = 4299        (read from the executing tier)
  Call stack: checkout <- main
  Exec pulse: price -> if(false) -> [charge]   (path the tier actually took)

Same function, compiled run (`jet run` / release binary):

  [ debugging: compiled process — paused at charge ]
  Watches:    total = 4299        (real process memory via lldb/DAP)

Same breakpoints, same UI, same protocol facts; the chip names the engine.
No live session -> wires dark, header "not running". Nothing simulated:
what glows is what the running engine did.

comparisons.note: Blueprint's exec pulse and watch values are real because the Blueprint VM IS the runtime — single-stepping the VM is single-stepping the program, so its glow never lies. The lesson is not "animate a pulse"; it is "debug the actual runtime." Jet's actual runtime is the compiled process, so the faithful equivalent of Blueprint's debugger is the native session (option A), not a separate interpreter that merely looks like Blueprint.
comparisons.code:
BP debugger: breakpoint on a node -> VM halts -> real pin values shown ->
exec wire glows the path the VM took (real, because VM == runtime).

comparisons.note: VS Code debugs the real process over DAP: it stops at real breakpoints, shows real variables, and steps real frames; it never animates a speculative execution path. Option A is the graph rendering of exactly this — the same DAP-class backend `jet debug` already has (tests/debug.rs), with pulse shown only at real stops.
comparisons.code:
launch -> hits breakpoint -> Variables pane shows real values ->
Step Over advances the real process; nothing is animated between stops.

comparisons.note: Scratch's block "glow" as a script runs is honest liveness precisely because Scratch is an interpreter — the glowing block is the one the interpreter is executing. That is the ONLY setting where option B/C's interpreter pulse is truthful. Jet is compiled and its debug target is the native process, so importing Scratch-style interpreter glow would make the animation a simulation, not liveness.
comparisons.code:
Scratch: the running block glows yellow because the interpreter is on it;
true there because the interpreter is the runtime.

decisions.title: Default jet prove execution semantics
decisions.gist: Choose what default `jet prove` runs and what pass, proved, incomplete, failure, and panic mean.
decisions.explainer:
Common producer law: TARGET may be one `.jet` file, package directory, or workspace directory. Resolution and lexicographic file order reuse `jet test`. Front-end checks run first. Per file, doctests run in source order, then the existing compiled test harness runs `#Test` declarations in declaration order. Parameterized `#Test fn` uses the existing seeded property generator and shrinker; plain `#Test` is unit evidence. Failed `require` or `require_eq` inside the test harness is a caught assertion: that test fails, later harness tests continue, final exit is at least 1. `panic(...)`, bounds/key stops, and failed `@Pre`/`@Post` contracts are uncaught runtime stops. They retain E3001/E3005, terminate that child with 70, mark declarations trapped in that child skipped with `prior_runtime_panic`, and the controller continues independent later files and budgets. A reached contract attaches to the producer invocation that called it; an unreached clause remains declared/not_observed. Deterministic budgets reuse the build/package producer; statistical budgets reuse the benchmark profile and pinned baseline producer. Order is front end, doctests, unit/property harness, deterministic budgets, statistical budgets. Front-end failure marks execution evidence skipped/prior_frontend_failure. Exit precedence after valid invocation is 101 ICE, then 70 if any child had an uncaught runtime stop, then 1 for user/static/caught-assertion/budget/policy failure, then 0. Exit 2 is malformed CLI before any report. No raw rustc message, generated-Rust path, backtrace, or type name may enter any view.

Every option produces the same semantic ProofReport envelope. Required fields are `schemaVersion`, `evidencePolicy`, `target`, `tool`, `result`, `exitCode`, `summaries`, `evidence`, and `diagnostics`. `target={kind:file|package|workspace,root,members:[{path,sha256}],inputSha256}`. `tool={jet,proofProducer,targetTriple}`. `result=pass|pass_incomplete|fail`. Every summaries member is required: `frontEnd={selected,proved,failed,skipped}`; `doctest` and `unit` each `{selected,passed,failed,skipped}`; `property={selected,passed,failed,skipped,generatedCases,shrunkFailures}`; `contract={selected,declared,observed,passed,failed,notObserved,skipped}`; `deterministicBudget` and `statisticalBudget` each `{selected,met,failed,skipped,unavailable}`. Evidence items require `{id,producer,kind,state,outcome,count,source,attachment,reason,property,contract,budget,diagnosticIndexes}`. `kind=front_end|doctest|unit|property|contract|deterministic_budget|statistical_budget`; `state=declared|checked|executed|zero|unavailable|skipped`; `outcome=proved|passed|failed|observed|not_observed|met|unavailable|not_run`; absent typed payloads are null. Property payload is `{effectiveSeed,caseIndex,generatedCases,shrinkTrace:[{name,value}],source:{path,line,column},toolchain:{jet,targetTriple}}`. Contract payload is `{marker:Pre|Post,site:{path,line,column},observation:reached_pass|reached_fail|not_reached}`. Budget payload is `{profile,kind:deterministic|statistical,observations,baselineId,limit,actual,unit}` with unknown values null.

Diagnostics are a required typed union which preserves product output, not merely a code. Every variant has `{type,code,severity,message,origin,span,caret,notes,frames,context,safeLocals}`. `type=front_end|producer|runtime`; `severity=error|warning`; `origin={stage,producer}`; span is null or `{path,startLine,startColumn,endLine,endColumn,sourceLine}`; caret is null or `{startColumn,width}`; notes is ordered text. Front-end and producer diagnostics such as E0965/E2901 preserve their exact What message, Why and Fix as ordered notes, source span, source line, and caret; frames/context/safeLocals are empty. Runtime E3001/E3005 preserve the Jet message, Jet source span/caret, ordered Jet frames, source context lines, and D-OBS2 safe locals `{name,type,value,redacted}`; they contain no rustc material. Evidence references diagnostics by zero-based `diagnosticIndexes`.

Every summary is derived from evidence, never independently counted. For frontEnd, doctest, unit, and property, `selected = proved|passed + failed + skipped` using the fields appropriate to that kind. Property `generatedCases` is the sum of evidence property.generatedCases and `shrunkFailures` counts failed property evidence with a nonempty shrinkTrace. Contract summary is `{selected,declared,observed,passed,failed,notObserved,skipped}` with `selected=declared=passed+failed+notObserved+skipped` and `observed=passed+failed`; each count derives from contract observation evidence. Each budget summary satisfies `selected=met+failed+skipped+unavailable`; all five counts derive from budget evidence. A report violating an equation is invalid. `zero` is successful discovery with count 0 and is complete. `unavailable` means an applicable producer could not start or lacked input; reason is `missing_baseline|missing_tool|unsupported_target|producer_start_failed`; state and outcome are both `unavailable`, matching D-JPROOF1. `skipped` is deliberate non-execution; reason is `prior_frontend_failure|prior_runtime_panic|not_executed_by_mode|fail_fast_policy`. Existing E0613/E2901/E3001/E3005/E0965 copy passes through unchanged. This decision allocates E2940 with registry-ready copy: What `required proof evidence is unavailable`; Why `the complete_required policy needs {producer}, but {reason}`; Fix `{producer-specific imperative action}`. Render example: `Error [E2940]: required proof evidence is unavailable` / `Why: the complete_required policy needs statistical budget checkout-p95, but no matching baseline exists` / `Fix: run jet bench src/payments.jet on the pinned profile to record the baseline`. It ships only after diagnostics registry, exact UI snapshot, `jet explain`, generated reference, and coverage satisfy I4.

One in-memory ProofReport drives terminal semantics and `--json` prints that exact ProofReport object, with no artifact metadata wrapper. D-JPROOF1 alone chooses `.jproof` serialization, path, identity, privacy, overwrite, and delivery metadata. Its artifact envelope embeds the byte-for-byte same semantic object as required member `proofReport`; artifact metadata is its sibling, never merged into or substituted for ProofReport. This ballot requires D-JPROOF1 to embed the exact ProofReport for pass, incomplete, caught assertion, producer failure, E3001, and E3005 before exit 0/1/70; it alleges no artifact path or wire schema. Usage 2, pre-identity load failure 1, and ICE 101 produce no valid artifact. No option invokes replay or a solver. `proved` is reserved for a fact universally discharged by the existing front end. Tests, sampled properties, doctests, reached contracts, and budgets say passed, failed, observed, or met.
decisions.story: Mara inherits a payment package with compiler-checked refinements, unit and property tests, doctests, `@Pre`/`@Post` contracts, and performance budgets. She needs one beginner command that runs existing evidence without calling sampled behavior proved. CI needs the identical typed report, including full Jet diagnostics, shrunk property evidence, skipped work, unavailable baselines, and a durable failed or panicked `.jproof` report.
decisions.inWild:
$ jet prove src/payments.jet
CHECKED  types, refinements, effects
PASSED   12 unit, 4 property, 3 doctest
OBSERVED 7 contract checks; 2 declared clauses not reached
UNAVAILABLE statistical budget `checkout-p95`: missing baseline
RESULT   pass; evidence incomplete
# D-JPROOF1 embeds this exact ProofReport before exit.
$ echo $?
0

# Exact current runtime stderr: no compile-diagnostic wrapper.
$ jet prove src/panic_worker.jet
panic: worker stopped
  --> src/panic_worker.jet:9 in worker
    |
9 |     panic("worker stopped")
    |     ^^^^^
locals: attempt = 3
RESULT   fail
# D-JPROOF1 embeds this exact ProofReport before exit.
$ echo $?
70

$ jet prove src/contract_worker.jet
@Pre contract failed: amount must be positive
  --> src/contract_worker.jet:3
RESULT   fail
# D-JPROOF1 embeds this exact ProofReport before exit.
$ echo $?
70

options.name: Layered evidence ledger
options.detail: Use `allow_incomplete`. Run every applicable producer. Complete success is pass/0. Passing available evidence plus unavailable, skipped, or merely declared evidence is pass_incomplete/0; expert CI may reject that typed result. Caught assertions return 1. Any uncaught E3001/E3005 runtime stop takes precedence and returns 70.
options.code:

options.detail: Use `complete_required`. Run the same graph. Zero selected evidence is complete and may pass. Applicable unavailable evidence remains typed unavailable but policy changes the overall result to fail, adds E2940, and returns 1. Caught assertions return 1; uncaught E3001/E3005 returns 70.

decisions.title: .jproof evidence artifact contract
decisions.gist: Choose the durable envelope around the exact ProofReport produced by `jet prove`.
decisions.explainer:
D-PROVE-SEM1 owns the sole semantic object: exact `ProofReport={schemaVersion,evidencePolicy,target,tool,result,exitCode,summaries,evidence,diagnostics}`. `.jproof` embeds that complete object under logical member `proofReport`; no parallel fact, evidence, outcome, diagnostic, count, or producer schema exists in this decision. The logical version-1 envelope has exactly six required members: `schema:"jet.jproof"`, `version:1`, 64-lowercase-hex `report_id`, `artifact:{path}`, `privacy:{absolute_paths,argv,environment,full_source,producer_transcripts,safe_locals}`, and the complete `proofReport`. Artifact metadata is only `schema`, `version`, `report_id`, `artifact`, and `privacy`. `jet prove --json` prints the A-canonical ProofReport plus one LF, not the artifact envelope, in every option. Human output projects that same object. D-PROVE-SEM1 decides semantic states, summaries, diagnostics, exits, and when reports exist; this decision only persists the object.

Version 1 target identity is exactly ProofReport.target. `kind` is file/package/workspace; `root` is the normalized project-relative selected root; `members[{path,sha256}]` is the complete sorted normal-loader input closure: Jet sources/imports, effective package/workspace manifests, lock data, generated sources, and build inputs that affect checked TIR. Each path is project-relative and unique; generated/logical inputs receive their stable project-relative loader identity. Members sort by exact UTF-8 path bytes. `inputSha256` is SHA-256 of each member's A-canonical JSON plus LF, concatenated in member order. Tool identity remains ProofReport.tool. Nothing outside ProofReport is allowed to alter target or producer meaning.

`report_id` is lowercase SHA-256 of the exact A-canonical ProofReport bytes plus one LF. It excludes all envelope metadata because none is semantic; path, privacy declaration, serialization option, and later signatures cannot change semantic identity. Readers recompute target.inputSha256 and report_id before trusting the artifact. The emitted artifact's separate SHA-256 covers every canonical artifact byte and is the boundary a later signing decision would sign, excluding only a future envelope `signatures` member/record; this ballot adds no signing or trust command.

Privacy happens before persistence, inside the D-PROVE-SEM1 report producer. The envelope cannot redact or add semantics without breaking report_id. It records the applied policy: absolute paths, argv, environment, full source, and producer transcripts omitted; D-OBS2 governs safe-local redaction already present in ProofReport. Project-relative paths, source spans/lines, semantic diagnostic messages, property counterexamples/shrink values, budget values, and any unredacted safe local present in ProofReport are disclosed. Users must treat `.jproof` as sensitive evidence. No unratified include-source, encryption, destination, overwrite, or inspection flag is introduced.

A-canonical JSON means UTF-8, no BOM, no insignificant whitespace, exactly one LF after a complete JSON value, object keys sorted by Unicode scalar value recursively, arrays kept in ProofReport order, and integers in shortest decimal; floats and negative zero are forbidden. Schema/extension keys must be NFC. User/source strings and paths preserve exact Unicode scalars. Escape quote/backslash as `\"`/`\\`; use `\b|\t|\n|\f|\r` and lowercase `\u00xx` for other controls; emit all other scalars as UTF-8, including U+2028/U+2029, and never escape `/`. Duplicate keys after key normalization fail. Version-1 readers retain unknown envelope and ProofReport members as complete JSON values, include them in canonical hashes/order, and losslessly re-emit them; unknown enums fail unsupported. Unknown major version fails E3613.

Artifact lifecycle is common except final-path policy. Jet canonicalizes the project, takes an exclusive mode-0600 project proof lock, creates new artifact directories mode 0700, and resolves every parent/final component no-follow. Absolute/`..` escape, symlink, non-directory parent, or non-regular final is E3614. A same-directory random temp is opened exclusive/no-follow mode 0600, fully written, file-fsynced, atomically committed without replacement, then parent-dir-fsynced before success. Unsupported primitives fail before writing. Failure removes only the owned temp. Crash leftovers are cleaned under lock only after reserved-name and regular/no-link validation. Cooperative runs serialize; exclusive temp plus no-replace prevents an uncooperative creator from being overwritten. No partial final artifact is observable.

E3611-E3614 are disjoint from sibling replay diagnostics and reserved here: corrupt/hash/canonical failure; wrong target; unsupported artifact version; unsafe path. Each exits 1. Malformed CLI remains 2, runtime stop 70, ICE 101. They must enter diagnostics.md, exact UI snapshots, `jet explain`, generated references, and coverage before shipping under I4.
decisions.story: Mara archives a successful refinement proof, then a failed property report. Six months later a reviewer must identify the exact file, package, or workspace inputs and Jet producer, recover the same ProofReport CI saw from `--json`, distinguish corruption from a proof failure, and know which sensitive values were omitted. Serialization may vary, but no artifact format may reinterpret, summarize, or duplicate proof semantics.

$ jet prove examples/features/types/refinements.jet
Error [E3611]: proof artifact is corrupt
 Why: its report hash does not match the embedded ProofReport
 Fix: move the corrupt artifact aside, then run `jet prove examples/features/types/refinements.jet` again
$ echo $?
1

Error [E3612]: proof artifact names a different target
 Why: its ProofReport root is `other.jet`, but this run resolved `examples/features/types/refinements.jet`
 Fix: move the other artifact aside, then run `jet prove examples/features/types/refinements.jet` again

Error [E3613]: proof artifact version `2` is not supported
 Why: this Jet reads `jet.jproof` version `1`
 Fix: use the Jet version that wrote the artifact, or move it aside and generate version `1`

Error [E3614]: proof artifact path is unsafe
 Why: `.jet/proofs/file/refinements` is a symbolic link, so Jet cannot confine the write beneath this project
 Fix: replace the link with a regular project directory, then run `jet prove examples/features/types/refinements.jet` again

comparisons.note: A versioned envelope binds exact subjects to a predicate without redefining predicate semantics. `.jproof` similarly wraps the sibling-owned ProofReport.
A run envelope preserves tool identity and complete structured results. JPROOF likewise persists the exact report rather than a second summary.
Recursive deterministic JSON gives report and artifact hashes a byte-exact boundary.

decisions.title: General replay capture invocation and .jreplay law
decisions.gist: Choose how users start replay capture while keeping one exact, private, deterministic .jreplay contract.
decisions.explainer:
Common law for A, B, and C follows. D-PROVE-REPLAY1 consumption stays exactly `jet prove <target> --replay <artifact>`; no option creates `jet replay`, changes `jet run`, or adds auxiliary out/encrypt/key/case flags. Each option chooses one complete capture invocation. Capture grammar is closed and parseable. Flag models use exactly `jet prove TARGET --capture` or `jet prove TARGET --capture=ARTIFACT`, and sensitive counterparts replace the flag with `--capture-sensitive`; TARGET is the sole positional before the flag, ARTIFACT exists only after `=`, and a spaced artifact argument is usage error 2. Subcommand models use exactly `jet prove capture TARGET` or `jet prove capture TARGET ARTIFACT`, with sensitive counterpart `capture-sensitive`; TARGET is first positional and optional ARTIFACT second, while a third positional is usage error 2. `--` is not accepted by capture forms. Relative artifacts are project-relative; absolute artifacts follow common explicit-path law.\n\nTarget selection reuses current `jet run TARGET` resolution without a replay-only selector. A `.jet` file is one runnable unit when current run resolution accepts its file entry, otherwise capture reports that existing diagnostic. A package directory selects its manifest's current default runnable target; a workspace directory enumerates current runnable member defaults in lexicographic package-name/path order. Package/workspace capture requires exactly one resolved runnable target after current selection; zero or multiple fail E3624 before build or program effects and list exact package, target, and entry paths. One invocation produces one run and at most one artifact. Capture first resolves target, checks source, computes the full reachable effect/native graph, validates ordinary invocation authority, privacy mode, cardinality, target support, and output destination, then builds. Capture never grants an effect: every ambient operation still needs its normal lexical gate and existing `--allow-*` invocation policy. FFI, native callbacks, dynamic loading, tasks/concurrency, wall-driven scheduling, Fs, Env, Exec, Db, Gpu, and any opaque call graph fail E3625 during preflight; Jet must prove absence before starting the child, never discover them after partial effects. Replay grants zero ambient effects and opens no clock, RNG, stdin, terminal, DNS, socket, file, environment, subprocess, FFI, task, or GPU boundary. It only reads the artifact and build inputs, injects records, and verifies requests/outcome; any attempted unrecorded ambient boundary is E3623.

The canonical bytes are: 8-byte ASCII magic `JREPLAY\0`; little-endian u16 major and minor; little-endian u32 canonical-header length; canonical-header bytes; zero or more frames; footer. Version 1.0 header is UTF-8 JSON with no BOM, ASCII field names sorted by byte value, no whitespace, no duplicate keys, strings escaped with JSON's shortest valid escape, integers as minimal base-10 JSON integers, no floats, and no null for required fields. User text is preserved as exact Unicode scalar values and never normalized; unpaired surrogates and invalid UTF-8 fail E3622. Schema paths are UTF-8 project-relative forward-slash paths with no empty, `.`, `..`, absolute, NUL, or symlink component; a non-UTF-8 project path is unsupported E3625. Binary values use unpadded base64url; signed/unsigned 64-bit values that exceed exact JSON integer range use lowercase fixed-width hexadecimal strings; floats use exact lowercase IEEE-754 bit-pattern hexadecimal strings, preserving NaN payload and signed zero. Required header fields are `schema`, `version`, `artifact_id`, `producer`, `identity`, `capture`, `privacy_salt`, `limits`, and `run`; unknown required fields/record kinds fail E3620. Unknown optional fields are permitted only under sorted `extensions` maps, are hashed, preserved by copy/export, and ignored by an older same-major reader. Binary prefix major/minor must equal header version major/minor byte-for-byte; disagreement is corrupt E3622. Same major with understood required vocabulary is accepted; newer major fails E3620 without guessing.

Normative complete v1 one-frame fixture is 1054 bytes and contains TimeWall kind 0x0001 at sequence 0. Full-file base64 is ``. Frame prefix hex is `010100000000000000000082000000`; canonical payload length is 130 and payload SHA-256 is `4f707c1f1646e3140e8568677986c97e9ba96b578b5458a6de84d127c37bea9d`; frame SHA-256 is `a6d276ec274673175c47deaaa8ba148859cebdf752efbdb5d89c2fbbe03f653f`; footer frame count is 1 and payload-byte count is 130; content id is `c10aee50b2a70ae2bfc02072`; footer SHA-256 (bytes before JEND) is `ba8d8e037dbb6e1cd90251551e40f6ebeb6a56df9c22249b6bbdc8126128b8ed`; full-file SHA-256 is `72bf4a0448f895b84993950ee59061d04ea3fe4378fdd05c4c679d717dae7090`. The fixture privacy_salt is the deterministic 32-zero-byte test value `AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`; production salts are OS-random. All values are normative and pinned byte-for-byte. Its normative test-vector path is `.jet/replays/fixture-c10aee50b2a7.jreplay`; production uses a random privacy_salt and therefore prints `.jet/replays/fixture-<artifact-id>.jreplay`, never this predetermined id. Every transcript below labels artifact content abbreviated. Frame kind registry is closed in v1: 0x0001 TimeWall `{site_id,call_id,unix_ns}`; 0x0002 TimeMonotonic `{site_id,call_id,ticks_ns}`; 0x0003 TimeSleep `{site_id,call_id,requested_ns,outcome}` where outcome is exactly `{"kind":"completed"}` or `{"error":"interrupted","kind":"error"}`; 0x0010 RandBits `{site_id,call_id,requested_bits,bits}`; 0x0020 IoRead `{site_id,call_id,stream_id,requested_bytes}`; 0x0021 IoChunk `{stream_id,chunk_index,bytes}`; 0x0022 IoEnd `{stream_id,chunks,total_bytes,outcome}` where outcome is exactly `{"kind":"eof"}` or `{"error":<portable error>,"kind":"error"}`; 0x0030 NetRequest `{site_id,call_id,request_id,method,scheme,host,port,path,redirect_index,header_digests,body_digest}` where redirect_index is u32 and header_digests is an application-order array of `{name,digest_sha256}`; 0x0031 NetDns `{request_id,addresses}` where addresses is an application-return-order array of canonical textual IP addresses; 0x0032 NetResponse `{request_id,status,headers}` where status is u16 and headers is an application-order array of `{name,value}` with exact text/bytes Jet values; 0x0033 NetChunk `{request_id,chunk_index,bytes}`; 0x0034 NetEnd `{request_id,chunks,total_bytes,outcome}` where outcome is exactly `{"kind":"eof"}` or `{"error":<portable error>,"kind":"error"}`; 0x00f0 Outcome is exactly normal/explicit exit `{"kind":"exit","status":i32,"stderr_len":u64,"stderr_sha256":"64 hex","stdout_len":u64,"stdout_sha256":"64 hex"}` or runtime stop `{"diagnostic_code":"<exact emitted Jet code>","exit_code":70,"kind":"runtime_stop","stderr_len":u64,"stderr_sha256":"64 hex","stdout_len":u64,"stdout_sha256":"64 hex"}`; runtime_stop preserves E3001, E3005, or any other existing exit-70 diagnostic code exactly and never relabels it; diagnostic_code is forbidden for exit and required for runtime_stop, so null is never encoded; 0x4000 GameEvent `{name,payload}`, where name is exactly `game.v1.action|game.v1.fixed_step|game.v1.backend|game.v1.budget`. Absent variant fields and extra top-level fields are forbidden; extensions stay under `extensions`. `site_id` is lowercase SHA-256 of length-delimited checked TIR hash, function stable id, instruction ordinal, and u16 kind. `call_id` is zero-based per-site invocation count. Io stream_id and Net request_id equal the start-frame sequence. Canonical Jet values use these complete tagged objects and no other keys: unit `{"t":"unit"}` requires only `t`; Bool `{"t":"bool","v":true|false}` requires `t,v`; signed/unsigned integer `{"bits":8|16|32|64|128,"t":"int"|"uint","v":"<minimal decimal string>"}` requires `bits,t,v`; Float `{"bits":32|64,"t":"float","v":"<fixed-width lowercase IEEE-754 hex>"}` requires `bits,t,v`; text `{"t":"text","v":"<exact Unicode scalar sequence>"}` requires `t,v`; bytes `{"t":"bytes","v":"<unpadded base64url>"}` requires `t,v`; list `{"t":"list","v":[<canonical Jet value>,...]}` requires `t,v` and preserves order; record `{"fields":[{"name":"<ASCII field name>","value":<canonical Jet value>},...],"t":"record"}` requires `fields,t`, each field requires exactly `name,value`, and fields sort by ASCII name. Missing, extra, or duplicate keys/fields, unsupported widths/types, and noncanonical values are E3622.\n\nPortable error is exactly one string from `interrupted|timed_out|would_block|broken_pipe|connection_aborted|connection_refused|connection_reset|not_connected|address_in_use|address_unavailable|permission_denied|not_found|unexpected_eof|invalid_data`. Each platform adapter has a pinned OS-error-to-one-string table. An OS error absent from or ambiguous in that table fails closed with E3625, terminates capture, and emits no valid artifact; raw OS numbers/messages are never recorded. TimeSleep permits only `interrupted`; IoEnd and NetEnd permit the whole registry.\n\nEach frame is u8 flags (bit 0 required; other bits zero), u16 kind, u64 sequence, u32 payload length, payload bytes, and 32 raw SHA-256 bytes over flags through payload. Numbers are little-endian. Sequence starts at 0 and is contiguous. Payload is the same canonical JSON law. Duplicate sequence/site/request ids, out-of-order frames, unknown required kind, noncanonical JSON, bad length/hash/footer, trailing bytes, or truncation is E3622. Footer is ASCII `JEND`, u64 frame count, u64 total payload bytes, then SHA-256 covering exactly byte 0 through the byte immediately before ASCII `JEND`; no footer byte participates. Artifact identity uses a separate deterministic content-id hash: serialize header-through-frames with `artifact_id` as exactly 24 ASCII zeroes, SHA-256 those bytes, take the first 24 lowercase hex digits, then serialize the real header and footer. A reader verifies both the zeroed-field content id and the actual-byte footer hash. Default final path is `.jet/replays/<sanitized-entry>-<artifact_id[0..12]>.jreplay`; sanitization is lowercase ASCII alphanumeric plus `-`, with other runs replaced by one `-`. Records are ordered by actual single-thread boundary order. Time and Rand values fit one frame. Io/Net byte streams use contiguous chunks of at most 1 MiB with stream id, chunk index, EOF/error terminal record. Limits are 100000 frames, 1 MiB per payload, and 256 MiB total artifact. Crossing a limit stops the child, deletes the temp, emits E3628, and emits no valid artifact.

A Time request records operation, stable checked-TIR site id, arguments, and exact returned wall/monotonic value or sleep completion; replay uses a virtual clock and never sleeps. Rand records operation, site, requested shape/length, and exact returned bits. Safe mode records Time only. Rand is raw nondeterministic data and requires the same sensitive consent as Io.Read/terminal and Net; sensitive mode records Time, Rand, Io.Read/terminal, and Net. Net outbound matching uses method, scheme, host, explicit port, path, ordered header-name/value digests, body digest, redirect index, and stable site; response records application-visible DNS addresses, status, ordered headers, chunks, EOF/error. Replay requires byte-identical request digests and consumes the next matching record; missing, extra, reordered, wrong-site, wrong-shape, or unconsumed records are E3623. No performance sample, span, allocation, scheduler event, lock event, wall-duration profile, source map, flamegraph, or OTel field may appear; those belong only to card #441 `.jtrace`.

Untainted data may still contain secrets. Every option's safe form refuses reachable Rand, raw Io.Read, terminal input, and Net before execution with E3627. Each option's explicitly named sensitive form is the sole consent path for storing their exact raw values; preflight prints authorities, host names, maximum bytes, residual disclosures, and destination, and requires typing the exact TTY phrase `capture sensitive`; non-interactive capture refuses E3627. Its artifact is mode 0600 but not encrypted: anyone who can read it can read stdin, response bodies, DNS results, paths, host names, panic text, and run metadata. Any value Jet proves secret or tainted in outbound URL userinfo, query values, header names/values, or body fails E3627 before the request is sent and no artifact is finalized. Every artifact generates a control-plane 32-byte OS-random `privacy_salt`, encoded in the header as exactly 43-character unpadded base64url; generation failure is E3629 before program execution. Header digest preimage is ASCII `jet.replay.v1/net-header`, one NUL byte, raw 32-byte salt, u64-big-endian name length, exact name bytes, u64-big-endian value length, exact value bytes. Body digest preimage is ASCII `jet.replay.v1/net-body`, one NUL, raw salt, u64-big-endian body length, exact body bytes. Each stored digest is 64 lowercase SHA-256 hex; replay decodes/length-checks salt, recomputes each digest, and divergence is E3623. Fixed-salt digest vectors use 32 zero bytes: header name UTF-8 `x-test` and value UTF-8 `abc` produce `da5c4be2ec0c362a0a7f2ecf6c989f6702f356b67223ba5e520c33c3dde111fa`; body UTF-8 `hello` produces `a0187a1248e5a0292177421845e354004354b6b9c59b985d9daed43d335c3a05`. Implementations pin both preimages and expected hashes. Because salt is stored and values may have low entropy, this hides plaintext bytes but does not prevent offline guessing; preflight states that residual disclosure. Stdout/stderr raw bytes are never stored: outcome stores byte length plus SHA-256 and replay compares both. Terminal still receives live stdout/stderr. Secret/taint proven at any stored inbound boundary fails E3627 even in B; users must supply sanitized deterministic input. Reports never print payloads.

This decision allocates disjoint codes: E3620 `replay schema version is incompatible`; E3621 `replay semantic identity does not match`; E3622 `replay artifact is corrupt`; E3623 `replay diverged at record {sequence}`; E3624 `replay target cardinality is not one`; E3625 `replay capture cannot model {operation}`; E3626 `replay capture lacks {effect} authority`; E3627 `replay capture refused sensitive data`; E3628 `replay capture exceeded its artifact limit`; E3629 `replay artifact could not be finalized`. Why names respectively the unsupported version, first identity field, byte/frame violation, request digest, candidates, unsupported effect/native/task/adapter, missing existing grant, raw/tainted field, actual vs maximum size, or exact path/race/filesystem failure. Fix gives the corresponding supported reader, recorded revision/toolchain, intact artifact, recapture action, single current target, source/target change, existing lexical and invocation grant, sanitized input/B choice, input reduction, or path action. E3620-E3629 exit 1 and each requires diagnostics.md exact what/why/fix, UI snapshot, jet explain, and generated reference before use. Usage is 2, captured/replayed E3001 panic 70, ICE 101.

After preflight, Jet creates a mode-0600 same-directory temp using no-follow exclusive creation, streams bounded frames, fsyncs content, writes/fsyncs footer, closes, verifies canonical bytes/hash/id, then atomically rename-no-replace to final path and fsyncs the directory. Existing final path is accepted only when its complete bytes equal the new artifact; Jet deletes temp and reports `already captured`. Different bytes at that path fail E3629; nothing overwrites. Default naming is content-deterministic. Explicit paths supplied by the chosen invocation must be project-beneath, no-follow, and nonexistent. Crash leaves only `.jreplay.tmp.<pid>.<nonce>`; next capture removes an old temp only after no-follow ownership/mode check and never treats it as evidence. A normal exit, explicit nonzero exit, or captured `runtime_stop` exit 70 finalizes the artifact. runtime_stop preserves the exact emitted diagnostic code: E3001, E3005, or any other existing exit-70 code; none is relabeled. CLI returns 0 for exit 0, 1 for explicit nonzero exit or replay/capture diagnostic, 70 for captured/replayed panic, 2 for wrong CLI, 101 for ICE. Authority/cardinality/privacy/unsupported/build failure, signal/kill, limit, recorder/finalization failure, and ICE emit no valid artifact. Capture streams child stdout/stderr and then prints artifact/outcome on stderr so program stdout remains exact.

Identity binds schema, Jet toolchain build id, Core ABI, TIR schema/hash, target triple/backend/profile, producer engine, entry identity, every checked source hash, package/workspace/lock/build-input digest, and authority/capture manifest. Replay requires exact source/build/TIR/target identity; mismatch is E3621. Capture adapters in dev and AOT are independent implementations over the same executable TIR: neither shells into or trusts the other. Semantic target identity (sources, lock/build inputs, checked TIR) is distinct from `execution_adapter`. Version 1 adapters are exactly `dev-tir-v1` and `aot-native-v1`. The only counterpart mapping is `dev-tir-v1 <-> aot-native-v1` for the same native target triple, ABI, profile, Core ABI, and checked TIR hash. Adapter identity may differ only by that mapping; semantic identity remains exact. Replay executes the recorded adapter first, then that mapped counterpart when supported. Each must consume all records and match outcome, and their outcomes must match each other. A target with no counterpart reports `parity: not available` and may reproduce but may not claim dev/AOT equivalence. Browser/WASM, native, and other targets never substitute a host backend. Card #238 `game.Replay.record("path.jreplay")` remains the source-owned game capture invocation and explicit path. It writes this same envelope with required record namespace `game.v1.*` for action snapshots, fixed-step timing, backend identity, and budget events owned by #238; general Time/Rand/Io/Net records are not duplicated for the same game fact. Its explicit path follows the same no-overwrite/finalization law, and `jet prove game.jet --replay path.jreplay` is the consumer.
decisions.story: Maya has one payment worker that panics after clock and random choices. She needs one bounded capture command, one private artifact, and an offline replay that proves the same outcome in the real dev and AOT engines. Dev must know exactly what bytes and authority entered the artifact; CI must reject stale source, corruption, divergence, unsupported effects, ambiguous package entries, and unsafe capture before claiming proof.
decisions.inWild:
$ jet prove src/worker.jet --capture
capture: Time only; Rand, Io.Read, and Net require sensitive consent
artifact: .jet/replays/worker-<artifact-id>.jreplay
outcome: runtime_stop E3001; exit 70

$ jet prove src/worker.jet --replay .jet/replays/worker-<artifact-id>.jreplay
identity: exact
records: consumed exactly
replay dev: runtime_stop E3001; stdout/stderr hashes exact
replay AOT: runtime_stop E3001; stdout/stderr hashes exact
proof: deterministic; dev/AOT equivalent

options.name: Paired safe and sensitive flags
options.detail: Beginner capture is exactly `jet prove TARGET --capture` or `jet prove TARGET --capture=ARTIFACT` and records Time only. Expert escalation is the paired `--capture-sensitive` form and records Time/Rand/Io/Net after common disclosure. Both inherit identical artifact, authority, lifecycle, diagnostics, and parity; privacy refusal is E3627, never E3626. Recommended: safe default shortest, sensitive intent script-visible.

capture preflight: safe Time only; authority unchanged
capture: exit 0
artifact: .jet/replays/fixture-<artifact-id>.jreplay

{\"capture\":{\"mode\":\"safe\",\"roots\":[\"Time\"]},\"privacy_salt\":\"<43 base64url chars>\",\"schema\":\"jet.replay\",\"version\":{\"major\":1,\"minor\":0}}

$ jet prove network.jet --capture

comparisons.note: rr records nondeterministic boundaries and replays offline. Jet records typed Core boundaries and Jet outcomes, not instruction/debug or performance-trace data.

HTTP cassettes repeat network results but often hide privacy cost. Every Jet option refuses raw Net in safe mode and requires an explicit sensitive interaction that discloses plaintext and guessable-digest residue.
A stable input journal can preserve deterministic game runs. Jet keeps #238 game payload ownership while sharing one envelope and prove consumer.

decisions.title: Opt-in solver backend and proof boundary
decisions.gist: Choose whether jet prove --lens solver runs a solver, exactly which obligations it may prove, and how bounded failure stays honest.
decisions.explainer:
Current law stays intact. D-WD12 makes solvers opt-in lenses; default jet prove TARGET never runs one. Existing sema remains authoritative for compilation, D-OOBPROOF1 codegen, and user diagnostics. The lens consumes immutable typed obligations exported after sema; it cannot accept source text directly, add syntax, relax a rejection, change TIR/codegen, or ask rustc whether code works. Codegen remains dumb (I3). All options are std-only path crates and add no external crate, executable, daemon, network call, or compiler dependency (I6). File/package/workspace resolution, identity, ordering, human/JSON parity, exits, and .jproof persistence are exactly D-PROVE-SEM1/D-JPROOF1.

An obligation is {id,kind,assumptions,claim,origin}. Its id is lowercase SHA-256 of target input hash, obligation kind, project-relative path, start/end line/column, and formula SHA-256, in that order; each exact UTF-8 component is preceded by its unsigned 64-bit big-endian byte length. Kinds are fixed_index_bounds, call_precondition, and function_postcondition. Assumptions may contain parameter distinct-Int invariants, function @Pre clauses, and affine equalities from a covered body. A call site may additionally use caller invariants and affine bindings dominating it. Claims are respectively: all assignments put an index in 0..N-1; every covered call satisfies the callee's linear @Pre; or every covered return satisfies its linear @Post. No option proves memory safety, effects, termination, concurrency, floating point, runtime I/O, sampled properties, or arbitrary Bool-returning functions.

Canonical formula bytes are one A-canonical JSON object plus LF: {assumptions:<bool>,claim:<bool>}. An affine atom is {affine:{constant:<minimal-decimal>,terms:[{coefficient:<nonzero-minimal-decimal>,variable:<stable-id>}]},relation:"le|eq|ne"} and means affine relation 0. Terms combine and sort by exact UTF-8 variable id; comparisons normalize over integers (for example x < 4 becomes x - 3 le 0). Boolean nodes are {op:"and|or",children:[...]}; flatten, deduplicate, and sort children by canonical bytes. not is pushed to atoms; true/false are {constant:true|false}. The common formula IR is quantifier-free typed propositions over mathematical integers: variables; integer literals; affine + and -; multiplication by an integer literal; comparisons == != < <= > >=; and Boolean and/or/not. Jet Int operations enter only when sema proves the covered operation cannot overflow; otherwise result is unknown machine_overflow. Unsupported in v1: variable multiplication, division/modulo, powers, bitwise/shifts, Float, strings/collections except a fixed-list length constant, uncovered calls, recursion, loops, branch-crossing mutation, effects, dynamic dispatch, unsafe/native/FFI, and assume_deterministic. Unsupported forms are unknown unsupported_formula, never compile errors.

A function-postcondition body is covered only when pure, nonrecursive, and made of affine immutable bindings followed by one return: no branch, loop, mutable binding, call, indexing, allocation, panic, or ?. A call-precondition site requires affine arguments and branch-free dominating assumptions. Fixed-index obligations use the existing fixed-list N and refinement facts.

Order is target member UTF-8 path, source span, kind, id. Every backend is deterministic: no wall clock, host load, thread race, random seed, portfolio, or map order affects results. Timeout means deterministic work-budget exhaustion, not elapsed time. Hard limits: 10000 obligations/invocation, 50000 normalized terms/obligation, 256 variables, 256-bit source literals, and 1000000 backend steps/obligation. Structural overflow returns unknown structural_limit with zero steps. Checked i128 implementation arithmetic overflow returns unknown coefficient_overflow; it never wraps. Presburger search uses a FIFO of canonical branches; branch atoms, variables, and candidate splits use canonical byte order. One step is charged before dequeuing a branch, generating one normalized inequality, checking one contradiction leaf, or creating one split child; the limit is checked before the charged action. Finite checking charges one step before evaluating one complete assignment in variable-name then numeric domain order. External kill produces no complete ProofReport/.jproof and retains no partial proof.

Backends return proved, disproved, or unknown. Proved requires a backend certificate embedded in solver evidence and validated by an independent std-only checker against the exact normalized obligation. Native-Presburger certificates are canonical trees: assumption{assumptionIndex}; and_intro{children}; linear_contradiction{multipliers}, whose nonnegative integer multipliers combine the branch inequalities to 0 le -1; or split{variable,pivot,left,right}, whose children add variable le pivot and variable ge pivot+1. The checker validates indexes, arithmetic, branch coverage, and every leaf. Native-finite certificates are {domainManifest,assignmentCount,rollingResultSha256}; the checker deterministically re-enumerates every assignment. certificateSha256 hashes A-canonical certificate JSON plus LF. Disproved requires a concrete integer assignment; Jet substitutes it using checked mathematical-integer evaluation and accepts it only if all assumptions hold and the claim is false. Invalid certificate/counterexample is ICE 101. Unknown reasons are unsupported_formula|structural_limit|step_limit|coefficient_overflow|machine_overflow. Unavailable is reserved for no selected backend/target, reason backend_not_shipped|unsupported_target. There is no fallback to property tests, execution, another backend, or rustc. Property evidence remains separately passed and never promotes solver status.

decisions.title: Proof lens vocabulary and semantics
decisions.gist: Choose the stable values accepted by `jet prove --lens` and whether they filter presentation or execution.
decisions.explainer:
Ratified law already fixes `jet prove TARGET --lens VALUE`, `--json`, and `.jproof`; this ballot chooses VALUE and lens behavior only. Bare `jet prove TARGET` is always the beginner default and means the complete proof run with the normal full human view. TARGET resolution is unchanged for file, package, and workspace. A presentation lens never changes target membership, source loading, producer order, evidence policy, result, diagnostics, exit precedence, report identity, or artifact lifecycle. Option C explicitly proposes execution selection and is exempt only from producer execution, result, and report identity; target, loading, diagnostics, exit precedence, and artifact lifecycle remain fixed.

Common safety law for every option: unless an option explicitly says its lens is an execution selector, Jet runs every producer D-PROVE-SEM1 requires in normal order. A presentation lens may suppress successful unrelated rows from the terminal, but it must always show the overall result and every failed, unavailable, skipped, or declared/not-observed item outside the selection under `OUTSIDE SELECTED LENSES`. It therefore cannot turn fail into pass, pass_incomplete into pass, hide E0965/E2901/E3001/E3005/E2940, change exit 0/1/2/70/101, or avoid work. For E3005 projection, `jet prove` owns the rendered diagnostic: if the runtime stop is not already a structured diagnostic, prove converts that owned contract-stop payload into structured E3005 before projection and pins the resulting CLI and UI snapshots. It must render the diagnostics.md What, full source location, Why, and Fix verbatim; it may not paraphrase the runtime string. Front-end failure and runtime panic keep the existing skip/continuation law.

`--json` always prints the complete canonical D-PROVE-SEM1 ProofReport, never a lens-filtered object and never terminal-view metadata. D-JPROOF1 embeds that exact same complete `proofReport`; selecting a presentation lens cannot change report_id or artifact bytes/path for the same run. Human output alone is projected. Machine consumers filter the full evidence by the ratified facet tag after parsing; no second machine schema exists.

Whichever vocabulary wins becomes the only required `facet` enum on every D-PROVE-SEM1 evidence item before those queued ballots are raised; schemas and fixtures contain only the winning values. It is semantic classification, not display metadata, and appears unchanged in `--json` and embedded `proofReport`. Under A or C, front-end obligations use `refinements`, `effects`, or `taint`, contract declarations use `contracts`, test results use `tests`, and runtime contract observations use `contracts`. Under B, every front-end obligation and contract declaration uses `check`; every unit, property, or doctest result and every contract observation reached during one uses `exercise`; budgets use `measure`; replay uses `reproduce`. Generic parse, type, and load evidence uses `all` under every option. Each evidence item has exactly one facet. Front-end production must be granular: one evidence item per discharged or failed obligation. Every evidence id is collision-safe and stable across presentation choices. Compute `claimSha = SHA-256(UTF-8(normalized checked claim))`, rendered as 64 lowercase hex ASCII bytes. The evidence-id preimage is the ordered five fields target input identity, kind, canonical origin path, canonical span, and claimSha. Encode each field as unsigned u64 big-endian byte length followed by its UTF-8 bytes, concatenate with no delimiter, then set id to the 64 lowercase hex SHA-256 of that preimage. Target input identity is the canonical workspace-relative input identity; kind is the producer obligation kind; canonical span is `start-line:start-column-end-line:end-column` in decimal with no padding. Pinned collision vector uses target `src/payments.jet`, kind `refinement`, path `src/payments.jet`, normalized claim `charge > 0`, and claimSha `4b540a89e2aa695859f78bffa0c55b3ab478b209481811434703b7de0a325e26`: span `14:3-14:19` gives `c9dada123c00380ab4bb14542d2700353a3fbb317f6152f65ec390706e4d915a`; same text at span `22:3-22:19` gives `2ba2d4c19daa50b7eb03ed32c7056ba583b81a66e4f7935dece9f6c993dcdacd`. The frontEnd summary aggregates proved, failed, and skipped counts across these split items; no parallel summary exists. A contract reached inside a unit, property, or doctest emits two linked items because one item cannot have two facets: the test item has `tests` under A/C or `exercise` under B; the contract observation item has `contracts` under A/C or `exercise` under B, and its attachment names the test evidence id. Each item keeps its own diagnosticIndexes and both contribute once to existing summaries. Summary equations remain derived from all evidence, not the selected terminal view. Pinned full fixtures use D-JPROOF1 A-canonical UTF-8: recursively sorted keys, arrays in shown order, and exactly one LF represented below as `\n`. Solver is the final evidence item. decisions.story: Mara runs `jet prove` on a workspace before release. The full result includes refinements, effect checks, taint facts, contracts, tests, budgets, and replay evidence. A beginner should run the bare command and see the whole correctness result. During a budget regression, Mara wants a focused terminal view without accidentally skipping a property test or hiding a contract panic. CI still needs the exact full ProofReport from `--json`, and the archived `.jproof` must remain the same semantic evidence regardless of which terminal lens Mara selected.

options.name: User-facing evidence facets
options.detail: Values are `all`, `refinements`, `effects`, `taint`, `contracts`, `tests`, `budgets`, `replay`, and conditionally `solver`; repetition unions them in that order. `refinements` owns range/refinement and bounds-discharge facts; `effects` owns inferred/declared effect and capability-bound facts; `taint` owns taint introduction, propagation, sanitizer, and sink facts; `contracts` owns `@Pre`/`@Post` declaration and observation evidence; `tests` owns unit, property, doctest, generated-case, shrink, and caught-assertion evidence; `budgets` owns deterministic and statistical budget evidence; `replay` owns replayability, artifact consumption, divergence, and parity evidence. Front-end compilation/type evidence and diagnostics have facet `all`; facet `all` is automatically included in every selected set and every machine filter, while `--lens all` remains the selection sentinel for the complete human view. Lenses are presentation-only. Recommended: names match what users are proving while preserving one full execution/report path.

LENSES  tests, budgets
TESTS   unit 12/12; property 4/4 (800 generated); doctest 3/3

OUTSIDE SELECTED LENSES

Error [E2941]: unknown proof lens `test`

options.name: Progressive proof layers
options.detail: Values are `all`, `check`, `exercise`, `measure`, `reproduce`, and conditionally `solver`; repetition unions them in that order. `check` combines refinements, bounds, effects, taint, and declared contracts; `exercise` combines unit/property/doctest execution and observed contracts; `measure` combines deterministic/statistical budgets; `reproduce` combines replayability, replay consumption, divergence, and parity. Evidence carries one layer facet; observed contract evidence belongs to exercise while its declaration belongs to check. Lenses are presentation-only. This gives four memorable stages but makes experts select a broad layer when they need one domain.
